( ) For further clarification on the terms self-trade, wash-trade and cross-trade, see ACER Guidance Note 1/2017.
Bidding ID
<biddingId>
Up to 50 alphanumerical digits Alphanumeric 50 12345abcdef
The field shall identify by a unique code the unit (asset) or the portfolio based on which the market participant was bidding the electricity at the OMP to buy or sell electricity for the reported transaction. The field is mandatory for transactions related to unit- or portfolio-based bidding. Unit-based bidding In specific auction and continuous markets, when market participants are required to bid the capacity based on the units the reported transactions involving unit-based bidding shall identify the ID of the unit in this field by populating in the field the string ‘UID’ followed by the ID of the asset. For example, if the Unit ID code (e.g. in Spanish auction and continuous markets) is identified as ABESC01, Data Field (44) shall be populated with the following value: <UIDABESC01>. Portfolio bidding In the case of portfolio bidding, market participants can bid at a portfolio level, this often implies the submission of complex bids or block bids. In such cases, the transactions record shall identify the relevant portfolio through its unique identifier as provided to the OMP where the transaction has been placed and/or executed. When reporting transactions involving portfolio-based bidding, Data Field (44) shall be populated with the string ‘PID’ followed by the ID of the portfolio, in a similar manner to the example for reporting the unit ID presented above.

• the total units of energy as 50 in Data Field (53) Quantity / Volume;

However, it is to be noted that this field is not applicable in the case of MAR and MTL order types reported in Data Field (16) Order type. If the price of the contract is set by a fixing index or a reference price indicated in Data Field (27), or by a deviation from a fixing index (+ or –), i.e. simple formula, this field is not applicable. However, if the price is set by a complex formula as described in Data Field (46), the final price information shall be reported in the field once available, by using Action type M. In the case of options, this field shall be used to report the option premium. In the case of spreads, when reporting an order, the price field should reflect the spread price, and this field should be populated with the spread value only for the leg for which the spread applies with a positive sign. Price formula
<priceFormula>
Up to 1000 alphanumerical digits Alphanumeric 1000 HGSG/HBS*+578HSH
The field is considered applicable if the price of the reported transaction is fixed by a formula. In such a case the applicable formula shall be described in this field in a precise manner. Complex formulas A complex formula-based price is understood as a price determined according to predefined mathematical expression by specifying how one or more fixing indices or reference prices are combined with agreed adjustments, discounts, coefficients or other parameters. In the case of complex price formulas, market participants should report a simplified version of the formula, provided a clear reference to all indices part of the formula is reported by specifying the fixed and variable components. All relevant indices shall be reported in Data Field (27) Fixing index or reference price. Schema field <priceFormula> is a free text field in the electronic format, however, for consistent and meaningful information on the price formula, reporting parties are expected to refer to the indications provided in Data Field (19) Price formula in Table 2. Example of a complex index: contract price = 80 % × baseload index + 20 % × peak load index + €1.50/MWh. Reporting requirements:
• Data Field (27) shall indicate two values: baseload index; peak load index;
• Data Field (46) shall be populated with the formula: 80 % × baseload index + 20 % × peak load index + €1.50/MWh. If complex indices are reported in Table 1, the record shall be updated with the final price by using Action type M once available. Simple formulas In REMIT transaction reporting, if the price is fixed by a single index or simply by a deviation (+ or –) from an index, it is considered a simple formula. In order to fix the price of a trade, market participants often agree on a difference (+/–) from the fixing index price that will be published after the trade occurs. In such a case, while the index is to be reported in Data Field (27), the differential from the fixing index shall be reported in this field. This implies that in case there is a difference from the value of the fixing index reported in Data Field (27), this field shall be populated with the agreed price differential from the fixing index, including the positive (+) or negative (–) sign respectively (e.g. + 0.05). The agreed difference (+/–) from the fixing index value may be expressed in currency (e.g. +/– EUR 0.05) or in percentage terms (e.g. +/– 0.1 %). If the price differential is reported in percentage terms, then the value ‘PCT’ shall be used in Data Field (49) Price currency and unit. Example of a simple index: TTF month-ahead price + €1.50/MWh. Reporting requirements:
• Data Field (27) shall indicate: TTF month-ahead;

• Data Field (46) shall indicate: + 1.50. When reporting simple formulas, there is no requirement to update the record with the final price once the index value is published/available. OMP transactions It may happen that the price of a standard contract that is admitted to trade on an OMP is fixed by a formula (i.e. applying a combination of multiple indices or a single index but embedded in a complex formula). In such a case, when reporting the transaction with Action type N, the price formula shall be specified in this field as indicated for the relevant contract advertised by the OMP. Once the outright price is known, it is essential to update the transaction report as a lifecycle event with Action type M by providing the outright price in Data Field (45). This requirement is not applicable if the price of the advertised contract is fixed by a single index or a simple formula as specified above. In the case of an option contract that is traded on an OMP or bilaterally, and the strike price refers to an index or a formula instead of an outright price, the option strike price formula shall be reported in this field, instead of Data Field (73). However, once the option strike price is known, it shall be reported in Data Field (73) as lifecycle event with Action type M. Bilateral trades For bilateral trades, if the price of a bilateral trade is fixed by a simple or complex formula but specifies a fixed quantity and delivery profile, it may be reported in Table 1. However, in the case of a complex formula, once the outright price is known, the trade report needs to be updated as a lifecycle event with Action type M by providing the outright price in Data Field (45). The same consideration shall apply for an option contract traded bilaterally with a strike price formula.
Data Field (47) Price in EUR/MWh
The data field is relevant for reporting LNG market data described in Annex III to the TRUM.
Data Field (48) Index value 48 Index value The field indicates the value of the fixing index.
<indexValue> | fixingIndex section in the OrderList/TradeList

This field identifies the value of the fixing index indicated in Data Field (27) Fixing index or reference price. The index value represents the value of the index at the time the contract was traded. The currency in which the index value is expressed shall be reported in Data Field (49) Price currency and unit. If the value of the fixing index is not known when the contract is traded, this field is not applicable. If the value of the fixing index is known when the contract is traded, the index value shall be reported in this field. For further guidance and examples on the reporting of transactions where an index or reference price is used to fix the price of the traded contract, see Data Field (27). Differential from the fixing index In order to fix the price of the trade, market participants often agree on a difference (+/–) from the fixing index price that will be published after the trade occurs, for example by the end of the particular day or month. In such a case the differential from the fixing index shall be reported in Data Field (46) Price formula. For more information, see Data Field (46).

units.t:
Price currency and unit
<currency>
<indexCurrency>
ISO 4217 currency codes and additional accepted Text 3 EUR values with three alphabetical digits: CHF = Swiss franc CZK = Czech koruna DKK = Danish krone EUR = Euro EUX = Euro cent GBX = Penny sterling GBP = Pound sterling HUF = Hungarian forint ISK = Icelandic króna NOK = Norwegian krone PCT = Percentage PLN = Polish zloty RON = Romanian leu SEK = Swedish krona USD = US dollar
This field identifies the currency to be considered for the unit of measurement of the value indicated in Data Field (45) Price and Data Field (87) Price/time interval quantity. As the value indicated in Data Field (45) indicates the price per unit of energy, the unit of measurement of the price refers to values indicated in Data Field (49) Price currency and unit and Data Field (56) Quantity unit per one unit of time. If Data Field (45) Price and Data Field (48) Index value are not reported, this field is also not applicable. If the transaction is priced as a percentage of the value of the fixing index (e.g. +/– 0.1 %), this field should be reported as ‘PCT’ for percentage. Example If the price currency in this field is populated with EUR and the quantity unit in Data Field (56) is populated with MWh/h, the unit of measurement of the value reported in Data Field (45) should be expressed in EUR/MWh.

Notional amount
<notionalAmount>
Up to 20 numerical digits in the format Number 20 53450.00 xxxxx.yyyyy with a maximum of five decimals This field identifies the total notional amount value of the trade. The notional amount shall always be reported in absolute value even if Data Field (45) Price is reported with a negative number.
The field is considered mandatory for all trades concluded on an OMP or bilaterally and executions reported in Table 1.
For orders and their lifecycle events, this field is not expected to be reported.
Calculation of the notional amount
The notional amount should be calculated using the following formula:
notional amount = price × volume × number of periods, where:
• price is the defined as the price of the volume as per Data Field (45);
• volume is the quantity of energy as per Data Field (53) Quantity/Volume;
• number of periods is the number of times that quantity is delivered (as derived from the delivery profile) as per Data Field (82) Number of periods.
This can also be calculated using the following formula:
notional amount = price × total notional contract quantity, where:
• price is the defined as the price of the volume as per Data Field (45);
• total notional contract quantity is the quantity of energy as per Data Field (54).
For example, a contract traded for a price of 50 EUR/MWh for a volume of 100 MW delivered for 24 hours (h) has the following notional amount:
50 EUR/MWh × 100 MW × 24 h = EUR 120 000.
Or for a monthly contract:
50 EUR/MWh × 100 MW × 24 h/day × 30 days = EUR 3 600 000.
Notional amount for index trades
Index trades may not have a value for the contract as this type of contract may not have a fixed price available at the time of the trade. Such trades may also include a differential from the published index value which is not available to the OMP. For example, + EUR 0.05 or – 0.1 %.
The index value may be published after the trading hours or in some cases days/weeks/months after the trade, for example, a month forward on an index where the market participant buys gas three months ahead from the trading date (a forward). The price of that forward will be set the day before the delivery starts based on the front month average price of the month before the delivery takes place. For example, a trade occurs in April for the delivery in July; the average front month (July) price in June is calculated on 30 June and the delivery starts on 1 July at the price of the average front month (July) price in June.
This field is not applicable to trades that do not have a known price at the time of the trade. The same applies to any contracts which have a floating leg, for example, gas/electricity financial swaps not reported under EMIR but reportable under REMIT. For example: in April, market participant A enters into an electricity financial swap contract for the month of July. Market participant A is the seller of the swap. Market participant A sells the forward fixed leg in April, and it buys the spot price (based on a reference price) in July. For the fixed leg, the forward price is known today, but the spot price is not known until the end of July. In this case, this field should be left blank. In some cases (e.g. trade at settlement), reporting parties may be able to calculate the notional amount of the trade and provide the notional amount by the time the REMIT reporting of the trade is due. Such information always provides added value to the transaction record.
Notional amount for option contracts
For the calculation of the notional amount for options, for the calculation of the notional amount the option strike price and not the option premium shall be used.
Data Field (51) Notional amount in EUR
The data field is relevant for reporting LNG market data described in Annex III to the TRUM.

Notional currency
<notionalCurrency>
ISO 4217 currency codes and additional accepted Text 3 EUR values with three alphabetical digits: CHF = Swiss franc CZK = Czech koruna DKK = Danish krone EUR = Euro EUX = Euro cent GBX = Penny sterling GBP = Pound sterling HUF = Hungarian forint ISK = Icelandic króna NOK = Norwegian krone PCT = Percentage PLN = Polish zloty RON = Romanian leu SEK = Swedish krona USD = US dollar OTH = Other This field identifies the currency for the value indicated in Data Field (50) Notional amount. The notional currency shall be provided in the unit as stored in the system of the reporting party. If Data Field (50) Notional amount is blank, this field is not applicable. Reporting parties may want to report in a major unit, for example, EUR rather than EUX for euro cent. The reason for reporting the major unit is to avoid unnecessarily large values. For instance, the price for NBP is quoted in pence per therm, but the notional value of the contract may be much bigger (e.g. a gas year forward is 365 days), so it may be more appropriate to have GBP 1 000 000 rather than GBX 100 000 000.

Quantity/Volume
quantity
<matched>
<visible>
<fullyVisible>
Up to 20 numerical digits in the format Number 20 100 xxxxx.yyyyy with a maximum of five decimals
Field description and cardinality
This field identifies the quantity or energy volume (delivery capacity) for the contract, i.e. the contract size or clip size. The value that shall be reported in this field is the volume per time unit, for example the number of MWh/h or therm/day. Reporting the quantity information for orders In the case of orders, this field is intended to represent the matched quantity and the quantity visible and available for trading in the order book. It is important to note that in the context of multiple matching events in the order’s lifecycle (i.e. due to partial matches) the matched volume should not be understood as a cumulative quantity matched over the lifetime of the order. It shall rather represent a matched quantity resulting from that particular matching event reported with Action type M as a lifecycle event. Example Market participant A sells 10 MW of electricity at 50 EUR/MWh on the day-ahead market, while market participant B sells 10 therms of gas at 50 EUR/therm on the day-ahead market. In both scenarios, the value of 10 should be reported in this field. The same applies if the contract is an hourly or monthly delivery contract. In the case of an order with a hidden quantity (e.g. iceberg orders), the overall quantity of the order should be derived as the sum of Data Field (21) Undisclosed volume and Data Field (53) Quantity/Volume. Price per time interval quantity If the transaction features different volumes for each delivery interval reported in Data Field (84) Load delivery intervals, Data Field (53) Quantity/Volume shall be left blank while the quantity information per delivery interval shall be specified in Data Field (85) Delivery capacity. Schema representation of the quantity information in the order report It is important to note that in electronic format in the OrderList, Data Field (53) Quantity/Volume and Data Field (21) Undisclosed volume are represented in the fields <matched>, <visible> and <undisclosedVolume> available in the quantity section. In addition, in the quantity section there is also a stand-alone field <fullyVisible> available. The below section describes the scenarios and the application of the different quantity fields in the schema.
• A group of elements with sequence fields <matched>, <visible> and <undisclosedVolume>: this section is to be applied in continuous markets when the reported order has a hidden volume (field <undisclosedVolume> is to be used) and/or the order is partially matched. In the case of the latter, the fields ‘visible’ and ‘matched’ are to be used, and also <undisclosedVolume> in the case of a hidden volume. This implies that this section of the quantity fields shall be applied in the cases of:
• order condition ‘HVO’, and/or
• order status ‘PMA’, and/or
• order status ‘REF’. For more information, see Section 5.2.4 of Annex I to the TRUM.
• Stand-alone field <fullyVisible> shall be used in all other cases, irrespective of the market type (such as continuous or auctions), when hidden volume or partial matching is not a feature of the reported order. The same considerations shall apply to the reporting of the total notional contract quantity in the schema.

units.b: Data Field (54) Total notional contract quantity
units.t:
Total notional contract quantity
totalNotionalContractQuantity TradeList
<matched>
<visible> OrderList
<fullyVisible> Up to 20 numerical digits in the format Number 20 1000 xxxxx.yyyyy with a maximum of five decimals
This field identifies the total notional contract quantity (TNCQ) of the transaction, including orders to trade. The field is mandatory for all transactions reported in Table 1, unless Data Field (74) Minimum/Maximum quantity and Data Field (75) Minimum/Maximum total notional contract quantity are populated. Calculation of TNCQ The TNCQ shall be calculated using the following formula: TNCQ = volume × number of periods, where:
• volume is the quantity of energy as per Data Field (53) Quantity/Volume or Data Field (85); Delivery capacity; and
• number of periods is the number of times that quantity is delivered (as derived from the delivery profile) as per Data Field (82) Number of periods. For the correct calculation of the number of periods, especially for products involving granularity less than an hour (i.e. 15-minute or 30-minute MTU), see Data Field (82). The TNCQ shall always be calculated based on the information on the volume and number of periods as provided in the respective transaction (i.e. order and trade) report. This implies that the TNCQ of an order shall change accordingly if any components of the above formula (i.e. the volume as defined in Data Field (53) and/or the number of periods) are modified throughout the lifecycle of the order. This also implies that that the TNCQ of the trade resulting from the matched order might differ from the TNCQ of the order originally placed. For example, a contract traded for a volume of 50 MW and delivered for 24 h would have the following TNCQ value: 50 MW × 24 h = 1 200 MWh. Or for a monthly contract: 50 MW × 24 h/day × 30 days = 36 000 MWh. Continuing this example, if the above contract was for delivery for 10 hours, the TNCQ would be 500 MWh (50 MW × 10 h). However, if the contract will be delivering for 10 hours for 30 days, then the TNCQ value would be 15 000 MWh (50 MW × 10 h/day × 30 days). Schema representation of the TNCQ information in the order report It is important to note that in electronic format in the OrderList, Data Field (54) Total Notional Contract Quantity and Data Field (21) Undisclosed volume are represented in the fields <matched>, <visible> and <undisclosedVolume> available in the totalNotionalContractQuantity section. In addition, in the same section there is also a stand-alone field <fullyVisible> available. For the correct reporting of the TNCQ information in the schema, see the guidance provided under Data Field (53).
Data Field (55) Total notional contract quantity in MWh
The data field is relevant for reporting LNG market data described in Annex III to the TRUM.

Option style
<optionStyle>
A = American Text 1 B B = Bermudan E = European S = Asian X = Exotic O = Other
This field identifies the option style, usually defined by the dates on which the option may be exercised: American, European, Bermudan, Asian or other. An American-style option can be exercised anytime during its life allowing option holders to exercise the option at any time prior to and including its maturity date. A European-style option can only be exercised at the maturity date. A Bermudan-style option can only be exercised on specified dates indicated in Data Field (71) Option exercise date or period. Option style ‘X’ for ‘Exotic’ is expected to be used for exotic options such as for swing, binary, barrier, trigger and window options. Reporting parties should refer to financial markets in order to identify the option style they need to indicate when reporting the relevant transaction under REMIT. ACER expects reporting parties to use the value ‘Other’ only in exceptional cases and to notify ACER via the REMIT Query Form in a timely manner in case none of the above-listed accepted values are applicable to the type of transaction/contract they intend to report. The field is mandatory for all transactions referring to option contracts as identified in Data Field (25) Contract type.

Option type
<optionType> optionDetails section in the ContractList P = Put Text 1 C C = Call O = Other
This field identifies the type of right the option holder owns. Value ‘P’ shall be indicated if the option is a put option and value ‘C’ shall be indicated if the option is a call option. In order to facilitate the reporting, reporting parties should refer to financial markets in order to identify the option type they need to indicate when reporting the relevant transaction under REMIT. If the option holder owns a type of right different from put or call, the value ‘O’ for ‘Other’ shall be reported in this field. Nevertheless, reporting parties are expected to consult ACER on the application of option style ‘Other’. The field is mandatory for all transactions referring to option contracts as identified in Data Field (25) Contract type.

units.b: Data Field (71) Option exercise date or period
units.t:
Option exercise date or period
optionExerciseDateOrPeriod
<optionExerciseDate>
<optionFirstExerciseDate>
<optionLastExerciseDate>
ISO 8601 date format Date 10 2026-01-29
This field identifies the date or period at or during which the option holder has the right but not the obligation to buy or sell the commodity or the underlying instrument at a specified price at a specified date or before. In the case of an American-, European- or Asian-style option, only one exercise date is expected to be reported. In the case of a Bermudan-style option, several dates or a period are expected be reported. Reporting parties should refer to financial markets in order to correctly report the exercise date/dates. The field is mandatory for all transactions referring to option contracts as identified in Data Field (25) Contract type.

Option exercise frequency
<optionExerciseFrequency>
X = One Text 1 W D = Daily W = Weekly M = Monthly S = Seasonal A = Annual O = Other
This field identifies the frequency at which the option holder has the right but not the obligation to exercise the option, i.e. to buy or sell the commodity or the underlying instrument at a pre-specified price indicated in Data Field (73) Option strike price. It is understood that European, American and Bermudan options can be exercised only once (in such cases, value ‘X’ is to be populated), while for swing options, for example, multiple exercise decisions can be made during the tenor of the contract. In such cases the applicable option exercise frequency, such as weekly, daily, monthly, etc., shall be indicated in this field as it is specified in the contractual terms and within the option exercise period reported in Data Field (71). The field is mandatory for all transactions referring to option contracts as identified in Data Field (25) Contract type.

Option strike price
optionStrikePrice
<value> optionDetails section in the ContractList <currency>
<unit> Up to 20 numerical digits in the format xxxx.yyyyy Number 20 125.98 with a maximum of five decimals
This field identifies the price at which the owner of the option can buy (in the case of a call option) or sell (in the case of a put option) the energy commodity or the underlying instrument as indicated in the option contract. If for an option contract that is traded on an OMP or bilaterally, the option strike price is set by a formula (e.g. for Asian options), the formula shall be specified in Data Field (46) Price formula. However, once the option strike price is known, it shall be reported in Data Field (73) as a lifecycle event with Action type M. The field is mandatory for transactions referring to option contracts as identified in Data Field (25) Contract type.

Minimum/Maximum quantity
quantity
<minimumMaximumQuantity>
Up to 20 numerical digits in the format xxxxx.yyyyy Number 20 100 with a maximum of five decimals
The field shall be applicable in case the transaction that refers to a standard contract traded on an OMP has a volume optionality specifying a minimum and maximum range for the volume to be delivered. An example of a contract with such a feature is a gas swing deal (e.g. swing options) traded on an OMP that specifies a minimum and maximum hourly quantity. Such a swing deal is typically reported as a transaction related to an option contract in the REMIT reporting. It is important to note that the transaction resulting from the option exercise is considered reportable with the final quantity and shall be linked to the transaction related to the option contract via Data Field
(39) Linked transaction ID. However, if a trade is concluded bilaterally that entails a volume optionality, it shall be reported in Table 2 together with the related executions in Table 1 by specifying the final quantity. Both minimum and maximum quantity information are to be reported in the relevant fields in the schema. The unit of measurement applicable to the quantity information reported in this field shall be indicated in Data Field (77).

Delivery point or zone
<eic>
<ean>
EIC Alphanumeric 16 10YCB-EUROPEU–8 EAN 13
The field indicates the EIC Y, Z or W type code representing the delivery point or zone of the reported transaction. Only EICs that are included in ACER’s List of accepted EICs are allowed to be reported in this field.
The reporting guidance on reporting the delivery point or zone for supply contracts in Table 1 and 2 is available in Section 2.3.
The field is mandatory for all transactions reported in Table 1.
Application of the EAN code
When reporting transactions related to local flexibility products, this field shall be used, in addition to the reporting of the EIC of the relevant balancing zone or market area, to report the locational information by reporting the applicable EAN code as the unique identification number that links the respective connection point to a specific user/address. For more information on the reporting of local flexibility products, see Section 2.1.3.2.

Delivery start date
<deliveryStartDateTime>
ISO 8601 date and time format using UTC Date and time n/a 2026-07-01T00:00:00.000Z 2026-07-01T00:00:00.000+00:00
This field identifies the date at which the delivery of the commodity starts as specified in the contract.
For more information on the lifecycle reporting requirements for this data field, see Annex I to the TRUM.
The field is mandatory for all transactions reported in Table 1.

Delivery end date
<deliveryEndDateTime>
ISO 8601 date and time format using UTC Date and time n/a 2026-07-31T00:00:00.000Z 2026-07-31T00:00:00.000+00:00
This field identifies the date at which the delivery of the commodity ends as specified in the contract.
For more information on the lifecycle reporting requirements for this data field, see Annex I to the TRUM.
The field is mandatory for all transactions reported in Table 1.

Duration
<duration>
N = Minutes Text 2 M HQ = 15 minute HH = 30 minute H = Hour D = Day W = Week WE = Weekend M = Month Q = Quarter S = Season Y = Annual O = Other
This field identifies the duration of the delivery period of the contracts represented in a generic way. This means that the field is not intended to specify the exact delivery date and time of the product relevant for the contract (as this shall be deducted from the data fields on load delivery intervals, delivery start date and delivery end date) but identifies the tenor of the contract according to the above-described general classification.
The field is mandatory for all transactions reported in Table 1.
Description of the accepted values
HQ = 15-minute. The granularity/intervals for the trading period specify quarter-hour blocks (15-minute MTU) applicable to orders and trades placed/concluded within SDAC and IDAs. See Section 2.1.1.2.
HH = 30-minute. The granularity/intervals for the trading period specify half-hour blocks (30-minute MTU) applicable to orders and trades placed/concluded within SDAC. See Section 2.1.1.2.
N = Minutes. The contract has a delivery in one day for less than an hour. This value is not considered applicable to electricity auctions.
H = Hour. The contract delivers for one hour or several hours only for one day (e.g. block hours). For gas within-day contracts (provided the delivery lasts for one day), duration ‘H’ shall be reported in this field given that for gas within-day contracts the delivery will cover the remaining hours in the gas day.
D = Day. The contract delivers for 24 hours in one day or for several days (e.g. electricity baseload products or delivery of natural gas for the entire gas day), but the delivery happens for less than a week. W = Week. The contract delivers in one day or for several days, but the delivery happens for less than a month. Value ‘W’ shall be considered also for balance of the week contracts.
WE = Weekend. The contract delivers for a specified weekend period.
M = Month. The contract delivers for an entire month or for several months, but for less than a year (e.g. monthly baseload, monthly peak-load products). Also, in the case of one hour of delivery on a daily basis for one month, the field should be populated with ‘M’. Value ‘M’ shall be considered applicable also for balance of the month contracts. For executions reported under the framework of Table 2 non-standard contracts, the industry practice typically determines monthly deliveries (due to the monthly invoicing), therefore value ‘M’ is reported in most of the cases when reporting executions in Table 1.
Q = Quarter. The delivery happens for an entire quarter or for several quarters.
S = Season. The delivery happens over a season, such as winter-season or calendar season.
Y = Annual. The delivery happens for one or several years (e.g. yearly baseload products).
O = Other. ACER expects reporting parties to use the value ‘Other’ only in exceptional cases and to notify ACER via the REMIT Query Form in a timely manner in case none of the above-listed accepted values are applicable to the type of transaction/contract they intend to report.

Number of periods
<NumberOfPeriod>
Up to 20 numerical digits in the format Number 20 0.25 xxxxx.yyyyy with a maximum of eight decimals
The field shall identify the number of periods (NoP) included in the delivery profile of the contract. The total count of the delivery periods shall be expressed in hourly resolution over which the contracted energy is delivered between the delivery start time and delivery end time reported in Data Fields (79) and (80).
Deriving the correct NoP is relevant for the calculation of Data Field (54) Total notional contract quantity. As indicated in Data Field (54), the TNCQ shall be calculated by using the following formula: TNCQ = volume × number of periods.
The field is mandatory for all transactions reported in Table 1.
Calculation of the NoP For the calculation of the NoP, hourly resolution shall always be applied. For example, for a monthly baseload electricity contract that specifies delivery for the month of January 2026, the value of the NoP to be populated in Data Field (82) is 744.
For products where the delivery interval is less than an hour, for example a 15-minute product for the supply of electricity, the NoP shall be calculated by dividing the delivery interval (e.g. 15 minutes) by one hour (i.e. 60 minutes). Hence, the NoP in the case of a 15-minute product (provided it delivers just one day) shall be equal to 0.25.
Early termination of the trade
If counterparties decide to terminate the trade early during delivery, it is important that the record sent with Action type C for the cancellation includes an updated value for the number of periods adjusted according to the cancellation date. If the early termination occurs before the start of the delivery, there is no need to update the information sent previously in this field.

Load type
<loadType>
BL = Baseload Text 2 BL PL = Peak-load OP = Off-Peak-load BH = Hour/Block Hours SH = Shaped GD = Gas-Day OT = Other
This field identifies the delivery profile of the contract. It is understood that the delivery profile, hence, the load type of the contract, is defined as per the definition of the OMP where the contract is admitted to trading or as agreed between the market participants in the case of bilateral trades.
The field is mandatory for all transactions reported in Table 1.
Description of accepted values
BL = Baseload. The contracted volume to supply electricity is delivered continuously for all 24 hours of the day. The delivery may last for a single day or for several days.
PL = Peak load. The product is delivered only during the peak demand hours of the day, rather than continuously, like in a baseload contract. Peak hours may vary by Member State, but a common definition in many European power markets is from Monday to Friday, starting from 07:00 or 08:00 until 19:00 or 20:00, respectively (excluding weekends and holidays). OP = Off-peak load. The product is delivered during all the hours outside the defined peak-load period. Off-peak hours depend on the market, but a common definition in many European power markets is from Monday to Friday, starting from 19:00 or 20:00 until 07:00 or 08:00, respectively, including weekends and holidays.
BH = Bour/block hours. The product is delivered in a predefined set of hours each day (fixed hourly blocks), being different from baseload, peak-load or off-peak delivery profiles.
SH = Shaped. A contract is considered to have a customised delivery profile, i.e. it specifies the amount of energy to be bought or sold in different points in time to allow the market participant to meet their specific needs.
GD = Gas-day. Natural gas is delivered continuously during the day, typically running from 06:00 in the morning to 06:00 in the morning of the next day. For within-day contracts where the delivery of the gas runs from a certain hour of the gas day until 06:00 in the morning of the next day, load type ‘GD’ is considered applicable.
OT = Other. The value ‘Other’ shall be used for LNG-related transactions. In general, ACER expects reporting parties to use the value ‘Other’ only in exceptional cases and to notify ACER via the REMIT Query Form in a timely manner in case none of the above-listed accepted values are applicable to the type of transaction/contract they intend to report. For the application of the correct load type for a specific product or contract, see examples included in Annex II to the TRUM.

Load delivery intervals
<loadDeliveryStartDateTime>
<loadDeliveryEndDateTime>
<intervalStartDateTime>
<intervalEndDateTime>
ISO 8601 date and time format using UTC Date end n/a 2026-07-01T00:00:00.000Z Time 2026-07-01T00:00:00.000+00:00
This field identifies the load intervals for the delivery of the product as specified in the contract. The field is mandatory for all transactions reported in Table 1. Reporting of the delivery profile in the electronic format The load delivery interval shall indicate the exact time interval when the product is being delivered under the traded contract the reported transaction refers to. When reporting the delivery profile in the XML, it is important to note that each non-interrupted interval of the delivery profile shall be reported in a distinct row of the XML file. This implies that the deliveryProfile section with the load delivery intervals (start date time and end date time) in the ContractList is expected to be repeated as many times for as many interrupted intervals are included in the profile of the reported product. An ‘interrupted interval’ means that between the delivery start and end date of the contract there are interruptions (i.e. breaks) in the delivery interval of the commodity. For example, a baseload contract with continuous (i.e. non-interrupted) delivery until the delivery end date is considered to be reported as one single interval since there are no interruptions in the delivery period. On the other hand, peak-load and off-peak-load contracts are to be reported by using multiple intervals, since the delivery is not continuous due to breaks between peak and off-peak times. The above-described reporting requirement shall be applied irrespective of whether the price and/or quantity is different per delivery interval. This implies that Data Fields (85) and (87) can be blank if the price and/or quantity are the same for each interval included in the contract (i.e. reported in Data Fields

(45) and (53)). Furthermore, in such a case, <intervalStartDateTime> and <intervalEndDateTime> are to be left blank in the OrderList and TradeList. For one load delivery interval with constant price and quantity, irrespective of how long the delivery lasts for within that load delivery interval, only one load delivery start time (i.e. when the load delivery starts) and only one load delivery end time (i.e. when the load delivery ends) shall be reported. Reportable time format for midnight and end of gas day The load delivery interval is represented in a date–time format in the schema. According to the ISO 8601 standard and the electronic format adopted by ACER, it is expected that when the delivery starts or ends at the beginning or end of the day (i.e. the delivery time refers to midnight), the time information shall be represented as 00:00:00. However, depending on whether a start time or an end time has to be reported for delivery intervals, different date information shall be adopted. When trading electricity, the delivery start time shall be reported as 00:00:00 on Day X if the delivery starts at the beginning of Day X. For the delivery end time, if the delivery ends at midnight of Day Y (i.e. end of the day of Day Y), the delivery end time shall be expressed as 00:00:00 of Day Y+1. For example, for a typical yearly electricity baseload contract, where the delivery starts at the beginning of 2026-01-01, the delivery start date and time shall be expressed as 2026-01-01T00:00:00.000+02:00. The delivery end date and time shall be expressed as 2027-01-01T00:00:00.000+02:00. When trading natural gas, the delivery start time for a gas day shall be reported as 06:00:00 on Day X, and the delivery end time shall be reported as 06:00:00 on Day X+1. For example, for a gas within-day contract where the delivery starts on 2026-08-01 at 06:00:00, the delivery start date and time should be populated with 2026-08-01 06:00:00. The delivery end date and time should be populated with 2026-08-02 06:00:00. Example of a yearly baseload product ContractList <deliveryStartDateTime>2026-01-01T00:00:00.000+02:00</deliveryStartDateTime> <deliveryEndDateTime>2027-01-01T00:00:00.000+02:00</deliveryEndDateTime> <loadType>BL</loadType> <deliveryProfile> <loadDeliveryStartDateTime>2026-01-01T00:00:00.000+02:00</loadDeliveryStartDateTime> <loadDeliveryEndDateTime>2027-01-01T00:00:00.000+02:00</loadDeliveryEndDateTime> </deliveryProfile>
Example of a monthly peak-load product ContractList <deliveryStartDateTime>2026-08-03T00:00:00.000+02:00</deliveryStartDateTime> <deliveryEndDateTime>2028-09-01T00:00:00.000+02:00</deliveryEndDateTime> <loadType>PL</loadType> <deliveryProfile> <loadDeliveryStartDateTime>2026-08-03T07:00:00.000+02:00</loadDeliveryStartDateTime> <loadDeliveryEndDateTime>2026-08-01T19:00:00.000+02:00</loadDeliveryEndDateTime> </deliveryProfile> <deliveryProfile> <loadDeliveryStartDateTime>2026-08-04T07:00:00.000+02:00</loadDeliveryStartDateTime> <loadDeliveryEndDateTime>2026-08-04T19:00:00.000+02:00</loadDeliveryEndDateTime> </deliveryProfile> <deliveryProfile> <loadDeliveryStartDateTime>2026-08-05T07:00:00.000+02:00</loadDeliveryStartDateTime> <loadDeliveryEndDateTime>2026-08-05T19:00:00.000+02:00</loadDeliveryEndDateTime> </deliveryProfile> (The similar pattern is repeated until the end of the delivery month.)
Different price and/or quantity per interval If a transaction has a load profile with different quantities and/or prices across the relevant time intervals, each distinct delivery interval must be reported separately within the same report. For instance, if the trade or order refers to a five-hour delivery profile, with a different price and quantity per hour, five different delivery intervals will have to be reported within the same report. In such a case Data Fields (85), (86) and (87) shall be populated to indicate the relevant information for the price and/or quantity per interval. Representation of the load delivery intervals in the electronic format In the case of reporting the same price and quantity in Data Fields (45) and (53) respectively for each load delivery interval, elements <loadDeliveryStartDateTime> and <loadDeliveryEndDateTime> shall be populated in electronic format. In the case of reporting different a price and/or quantity for each load delivery interval by using Data Fields (85) and (87), fields <intervalStartDateTime> and <intervalEndDateTime> shall be populated. Representation of the interval in case of a clock change In case of a long clock change, as there is no unique identification of the traded period, reporting parties shall report the same interval twice. ACER will then consider in chronological order the two intervals reported and thus refer to the third and fourth hour of the day, respectively. Example of Data Field (84) reported on the long clock change: 00:00/01:00 – first hour 01:00/02:00 – second hour 02:00/03:00 – third hour 02:00/03:00 – fourth hour
Data Field (85) Delivery capacity
quantity
<value>
Up to 20 numerical digits in the format Number 20 10 xxxxx.yyyyy with a maximum of five decimals
This field identifies the delivery capacity (i.e. quantity/volume of energy) for each delivery interval if the delivery capacity is different for each delivery interval reported in Data Field (84) Load delivery intervals.
If the delivery capacity is the same for each delivery interval, then this field is not applicable since in such a case the quantity/volume information is to be reported in Data Field (53) Quantity/Volume.
The applicable unit of measurement for the quantity information reported in this field shall be indicated in Data Field (86).
fn: 85 Delivery capacity The field indicates the number of units included in the transaction, per delivery time interval.

units.b: Data Field (86) Quantity unit used in field 85
units.t:
Quantity unit used in field 85
quantity
<unit>
KW Text 2 to 9 MW KWh/h KWh/d MW MWh/h MWh/d GW GWh/h GWh/d Therm/d KTherm/d MTherm/d cm/d mcm/d tcm/d Btu/d MMBtu/d MJ/d 100MJ/d MMJ/d GJ/d
This field identifies the unit used for the quantity/volume reported in Data Field (85) Delivery capacity. The field is mandatory when Data Field (85) is reported with volume information.

Price/time interval quantity
priceTimeIntervalQuantity
<value>
Up to 20 numerical digits in the format Number 20 50.25 xxxx.yyyyy with a maximum of five decimals
This field identifies the price for the amount of energy to buy or sell at each time interval if the price differs among the delivery intervals reported in Data Field (84) Load delivery intervals.
If the price is the same for each delivery interval, this field is not applicable, given that the price information shall be reported in Data Field (45) Price in such cases.
The price reported in this field shall be expressed in the price currency indicated in Data Field (49) Price currency and unit.
It is important to note that if several intervals are reported with a different price and/or quantity, in the REMIT report the chronological order (i.e. time sequence) of the interval shall be maintained. This means that it is not allowed to group together several non-consecutive intervals that have the same price and/or quantity.
Example If Data Field (84) Load delivery intervals indicates two delivery intervals: 9:00 to 12:00 and 12:00 to 15:00 and Data Field (85) Delivery capacity indicates two capacities, for example 10 MW (for delivery 9:00 to 12:00) and 20 MW (for delivery 12:00 to 15:00), then this field shall be used for reporting different prices per unit of energy per each block, for example EUR 50/MWh (for delivery 9:00 to 12:00) and EUR 55/MWh (for delivery 12:00 to 15:00). If the price per unit of energy for the two blocks is the same, then the price should be reported in Data Field (45) Price, and not in this field.

Action type
<actionType>
N = New Text 1 N M = Modify E = Error C = Cancel
This field identifies the type of action representing a lifecycle event involving the transaction that is being reported.
The requirements for reporting lifecycle events related to transactions reportable in Table 1 are described in detail in Annex I to the TRUM.
The field is mandatory for all transactions reported in Table 1.
Description of the accepted values
Action type N (new) always indicates the first event in any transaction’s lifecycle. This implies that the first order or trade record shall always be reported with Action type N. The following corresponding record with Action type M, C or E can be accepted by ARIS only if a record with Action type N had been successfully reported previously. Action type M (modify) shall be adopted in case there is a modification of the previously submitted record, which represents a business event (triggered by a business decision or it is a result of a business event).
Action type C (cancel) indicates the last event in the transaction sequence as triggered by a business decision or as a result of a business event, for example when an order from the order book is permanently withdrawn or an outstanding trade is terminated early due to the change in the ACER code of the counterparty (i.e. novation), Action type C shall be reported.
Action type E (error) shall be used if the reporting party needs to indicate that the previously submitted record was erroneously reported, meaning that it was incorrect. Any correction to the already reported information using Action type E will result in a logical deletion (i.e. invalidation) of the corresponding record, which was previously successfully reported. It will, however, not delete the previously reported record from the ARIS database. Reporting an event with Action type E cannot be the result of a business decision, for example to change the economic values, such as price or quantity.
For further information on the application of the different action types, see Annex I to the TRUM.

units.b: Data Field (1) ID of the market participant being a counterparty to the contract
units.t:
ID of the market participant being a counterparty to the contract
<idOfMarketParticipant>
ACER code Alphanumerical 12 A0643278W.EU LEI 20 1a2b3c4d5e6f7g8e9f0h BIC 11 ACERSILJ500 EIC 16 21X000EUROPEU–8 GLN/GS1 code 13 a1b2c3d4e5f6g
This field aims to capture the ID of the market participant on whose behalf the bilateral contract is reported.
The field is mandatory for all contracts reported in Table 2.
Definition of a market participant from the reporting perspective
REMIT uses the term market participant, and EMIR uses the term counterparty to identify the reporting party. In the REMIT reporting framework, the term counterparty is considered as the other market participant with whom the reporting market participant identified in field (1) enters a transaction. The other market participant is identified in Data Field (3).
The registration of market participants with the relevant NRA will result in an ACER code. However, if a third party is reporting on behalf of the market participant, the ACER code may not be known. If the ACER code has not been provided by the market participant to the third party reporting on behalf of the market participant, one of the alternative codes listed above shall be used; otherwise, the report will be rejected as invalid.
Market participants are required to register with their relevant NRA. During the registration process, the market participant is required to provide all codes listed as accepted values in Data Field (1), if available. As a result of the registration process, the market participant will be registered in CEREMP and will receive an ACER code.
ACER code of the market participant
For REMIT reporting purposes, the ACER code is the preferred code to be used in the transaction record to identify the market participant, but all the other codes may also be used. If a market participant is already using the LEI for EMIR reporting, that market participant may also use the LEI code for REMIT reporting as long as the LEI has been provided to the NRAs during the registration process. If a market participant is using an ACER code, its counterparty may use that code to verify the identity of the market participant in the European register of market participants published by ACER and available on the REMIT Portal.

Reporting entity ID

6 | Field identifier | Description
Beneficiary ID
<beneficiaryIdentification>
ACER code Alphanumeric 12 A0643278W.EU LEI 20 1a2b3c4d5e6f7g8e9f0h BIC 11 ACERSILJ500 EIC 16 21X000EUROPEU–8 GLN/GS1 code 13 a1b2c3d4e5f6g
This field indicates the ID of the beneficiary of the bilateral contract in case it is executed by another market participant on behalf of a final beneficiary.
The field is always mandatory when the market participant identified in Data Field (1) is not the final beneficiary to the contract. If the beneficiary of the contract is not counterparty to this agreement, the reporting counterparty has to identify the beneficiary by a unique code in this field. In such a case, the trading capacity of the market participant in field 1 shall be identified with ‘A’ for ‘Agent’.
If the beneficiary of the bilateral contract is the market participant identified in Data Field (1), this field is not considered applicable.
For example, if party B is trading on behalf of party C, then party C is the beneficiary, and party B is acting on behalf of party C. As party B enters into a bilateral contract on wholesale energy products, party B is a market participant.
Bilateral contracts with a beneficiary may look like a contract in which market participant A sells to market participant B, with market participant C as the beneficiary. In these cases, ACER will receive one reported non-standard contract: market participant A sells to market participant B, with market participant C identified in Data Field (7) as the beneficiary.
However, a bilateral contract may involve multiple parties. For example, if a bilateral contract is signed between market participant A and market participant B, there may be other trades between (B) and (C) and (D) to represent how they split the value of the trade between (A) and (B).

units.b: Data Field (8) Trading capacity of the market participant in field 1
units.t:
Trading capacity of the market participant in field 1
<tradingCapacity>
P = Principal Text 1 P A = Agent
This field identifies the trading capacity of the market participant identified in Data Field (1).
The field is mandatory for all bilateral contracts reported in Table 2.
If the market participant is acting on its own behalf, this field shall be populated with ‘P’ for ‘Principal’.
If the market participant is acting on behalf of a third party as an agent, this field shall be populated with ‘A’ for ‘Agent’, and the beneficiary identification needs to be reported in Data Field (6).

Buy/sell indicator
<buySellIndicator>
B = Buy Text 1 B S = Sell C = Buy and Sell
The buy/sell indicator indicates whether the market participant is reporting the non-standard contract for the buying or selling of the commodity. ‘B’ shall be indicated for ‘buy’ and ‘S’ shall be indicated for ‘sell’ from the perspective of the reporting market participant, or from the perspective of the client in the case of an agent transaction (e.g. involving an executing broker).
The field is mandatory for all contracts reported in Table 2.
Reporting the buy/sell indicator in the case of derivatives
For derivatives that have not been reported under EMIR, and are therefore reported under REMIT, the following logic should apply for the reporting of this data field: for example, in the case of a fixed-to-floating derivative, if market participant A buys a swap, then market participant A pays a fixed price and market participant B pays a floating price. This means that market participant A receives the floating leg and market participant B receives the fixed leg. In the case of a floating-to-floating derivative, if market participant A buys a swap, market participant A pays the floating price of the first leg (or index) and market participant B pays the floating price of the second leg (or second index). In this case, the two legs (indices) of the swap should be sorted alphabetically.
If market participant A and market participant B enter into a swap agreement in which the financial settlement is the difference between two floating indices, ‘XYZ index’ and ‘ABC index’, market participant A is the buyer of the swap if it pays the floating price of ABC index and receives the floating price of XYZ index, while market participant B is the seller of the swap, as it receives the floating price of ABC index and pays the floating price of XYZ index.
Purchase-seller agreements
In ACER’s view, purchase-seller agreements are considered as non-standard contracts with undefined price and/or quantity; hence, they are reported in Table 2. Such a bilateral contract should be reported either as one contract, with ‘C’ indicated for the buy/sell indicator in Data Field (10), or as two separate contracts, one reported as ‘B’ for ‘buy’ and the other as ‘S’ for ‘sell’, provided the meaning of the two reports is the same. Any resulting execution concluded under the framework of the Table 2 non-standard contract should be reported in Table 1.

Contract ID
<contractId>
Up to 100 alphanumerical digits Alphanumeric 100 AGHDN15832839
This field identifies the unique contract ID as assigned by the two market participants being counterparties to the contract to be reported. The contract ID must be the same for the two sides (buy and sell) of the contract and shall remain unique throughout the lifecycle of the contract.
The field is mandatory for all contracts reported in Table 2.

Contract date
<contractDate>
ISO 8601 date and time format using UTC Date and time n/a 2026-07-29T16:30:00Z
This field identifies the date at which the bilateral contract was agreed between the counterparties. The field must reflect the actual date as a string representation of the ISO 8601 date and time format.
The reportable date of the contract is the date of the first binding agreement.
The field is mandatory for all contracts reported in Table 2.

Contract type
<contractType>
FW = Forward style contract Text 5 FW OP = Option style contract OP_FW = Option on a forward OP_FU = Option on a future OP_SW = Option on a swap SP = Spread SW = Swap OT = Other
Applicable to PPAs:
SO_PPA = Spot contract concluded under a PPA
FW_PPA = Forward contract concluded under a PPA
FU_PPA = Future contract concluded under a PPA
OP_PPA = Option contract concluded under a PPA
SP_PPA = Spread contract concluded under a PPA
SW_PPA = Swap contract concluded under a PPA
This field identifies the type of contract that is reported in Table 2 as a non-standard contract.
For bilateral contracts, a forward-style contract refers to the forward style, which also includes spot contracts. Market participants should not understand forward style as a sort of derivative contract, but rather as the style of the contract itself, i.e. for physical delivery at a later date. ‘OT’ means that ACER expects reporting parties to use the value ‘other’ only in exceptional cases and to notify ACER in a timely manner via the REMIT Query Form in case none of the accepted values listed above are applicable to the type of transaction or contract that they intend to report. The field is mandatory for all contracts reported in Table 2. Reporting non-standard contracts related to spreads
When trading a spread under the framework of a Table 2 non-standard contract, Data Field (12) is expected to be populated with ‘SP’ for ‘Spread’ for both legs (e.g. for the electricity leg and for the gas leg in the case of a spark spread). In the case of execution, the Table 1 report should indicate the contract type of the underlying contracts, for example ‘FW’ in the case of forward-style contracts.

Energy commodity
<energyCommodity>
EL = Electricity Text 2 NG
NG = Gas
LG = Liquified natural gas
This field identifies the energy commodity of the product delivered: natural gas, liquefied natural gas or electricity. Other commodities, such as emissions rights, coal, oil, etc., are out of the scope of REMIT.
Spreads are not considered commodities. Clean and dirty spark spreads – trades that involve both electricity and gas – have to be reported separately, unless the contract itself includes both commodities, in which case both gas and electricity should be reported in this field.
Such clean and dirty dark spreads that involve electricity, coal and emissions should be reported as an electricity contract. Contracts related to coal and emissions are not considered wholesale energy products and are thus not reportable under REMIT.
The field is mandatory for all contracts reported in Table 2.

Linked transaction ID
<linkedTransactionID>
Up to 100 alphanumerical digits Alphanumeric 100 1234567890abcdefrgf
This field shall indicate if two or more bilateral contracts and/or transactions are linked to each other due to a specific contractual arrangement or business agreement. In such cases, the contract ID of the related non-standard contract already reported in Data Field (10) in Table 2 or the UTI of the bilateral trade reported in Data Field (38) in Table 1 shall be populated in this field.
The linked transaction ID is considered applicable in the following (non-exhaustive) list of scenarios.
1. When bilateral contracts belong to the same option, spread or swap trading strategy (e.g. butterfly, condor), the contract ID or the UTI of the related bilateral contract or trade shall be reported in this field.
2. When two or more contracts are contractually bundled into a single corporate PPA, the two contracts should be linked to each other via this field. For example, corporate PPAs may be constructed in a sleeved structure where one party acts as an intermediary between the generator and the final buyer. In this case, each leg of the bundled contract shall be reported separately and linked via the linked transaction ID to reflect their contractual relationship.
3. If a purchase-seller agreement is reported as two separate non-standard contracts in Table 2 (i.e. one for the buy leg and one for the sell leg), the contract ID of the other leg shall be reported in this field.

units.b: Data Field (15) Type of generation asset
units.t:
Type of generation asset
<genAssetType>
SLR = Solar Text 3 SLR
HDR = Hydro
ONW = Onshore Wind
OFW = Offshore Wind
BIM = Biomass
NUC = Nuclear
NAG = Natural gas
COL = Coal
OIL = Oil
PFL = Portfolio
HRE = Hybrid Renewable
This field is applicable to PPAs to identify the underlying generation asset that is responsible for producing the energy to be delivered.
The field is mandatory when the contract type reported in Data Field (12) refers to a PPA featuring the reported non-standard contract. Description of accepted values
When the generation of the energy is carried out by a single asset type, one of the following values shall be reported: solar, hydro, onshore wind, offshore wind, biomass or nuclear. Fossil-fuelled assets are split into natural gas, oil and coal.
Asset type ‘PFL’ for ‘Portfolio’ is expected to be reported in case the PPA aggregates the output of multiple generation assets of different types, which may include both renewable (e.g. solar, hydro, onshore wind, offshore wind, biomass) and non-renewable sources (i.e. nuclear or fossil).
Asset type ‘HRE’ for ‘Hybrid renewables’ shall be indicated if the PPA is linked to a renewable generation asset combined with an energy storage component (e.g. solar and battery, or wind and battery), where the energy input is derived exclusively from renewable sources.
If the reportable PPA is not linked to a specific generation asset, this field is not applicable.

Underlying mechanisms
<contractUnder>
SUB = Subsidy Text 3 Subsidy
REL = Release
GOO = Guarantees of origin
This field shall identify the mechanisms or schemes impacting the formation of the contract. The field is considered particularly applicable to PPAs that may benefit from specific regulatory, financial or certification schemes. Nevertheless, the field may be applied to other non-standard contracts as well.
The field is mandatory when the contract type reported in Data Field (12) refers to a PPA featuring the reported non-standard contract in case there is an underlying mechanism in place.
Description of accepted values
When reporting a PPA in Table 2, one of the following mechanism/schemes are expected to be flagged in the report, if applicable:
• subsidy schemes (‘SUB’) (e.g. market premia, contracts for differences, capacity mechanisms, state-backed guarantees);
• release programmes (‘REL’) (e.g. gas release programmes, regulated capacity auctions);
• guarantees of origin (‘GOO’) (certification of energy origin). When reporting the price formula for non-standard contracts involving guarantees of origin, the reported formula in Data Field (19) is not expected to have a reference to guarantees of origin as long as they are not factored into the pricing formulation of the energy.
In case more than one underlying mechanism is applicable to the reported PPA, all mechanisms shall be indicated in this field, facilitated by the repeatable field in the schema.
Example
If a wind farm has a PPA supported by a feed-in tariff, this field should indicate ‘SUB’ to reflect that the contract was concluded under a subsidy scheme. If the agreement is also backed by guarantees of origin, value ‘GOO’ is also expected to be reported.

units.b: Data Field (17) Type of Power Purchase Agreement (PPA)
units.t:
No. | Field Identifier | Description
Type of Power Purchase Agreement (PPA)
<PPAType>
BL = Baseload Text 2 BL
PP = Pay as produced
PF = Pay as forecasted
PN = Pay as nominated
PC = Pay as consumed
FH = Fixed hourly profile
DP = Dynamic PPA
OT = Other
This field identifies the contractual structure of a PPA by specifying how the electricity delivery and the related payments are structured.
The field is mandatory when the contract type reported in Data Field (12) refers to a PPA featuring the reported non-standard contract. If several types apply to the reported contract, all relevant values shall be indicated facilitated by the repeatable field in the schema.
Description of accepted values
BL = Baseload. The buyer receives a constant, predetermined volume of electricity over the contract period. PP = Pay as produced. The buyer receives all electricity generated by the asset, with volume varying based on real-time production.
PF = Pay as forecasted. The buyer receives electricity based on a forecasted production schedule, with potential adjustments if actual generation differs.
PC = Pay as consumed. The buyer pays for the electricity based on their metered consumption.
PN = Pay as nominated. The buyer receives the electricity based on the pre-agreed nominations.
FH = Fixed hourly profile. The contract specifies a predefined delivery profile with fixed hourly quantities.
DP = Dynamic PPA. The delivery profile adjusts based on market signals, demand, or price triggers. OT = Other. ACER expects reporting parties to use the value ‘Other’ only in exceptional cases and to notify ACER in a timely manner via the REMIT Query Form in case none of the accepted values listed above are applicable to the type of transaction or contract that they intend to report.

Delivery terms
<deliveryTerms>
DES Text 3 DES
FOB
OTH
This field is applicable to contracts for the supply of LNG (typically LNG portfolio-type contracts, as described in Section 2.2.3) and shall identify the terms of the delivery, as specified in the contract, by referring to the respective industry standard, such as Incoterms (International Commercial Terms). In ACER’s understanding, supply contracts for the purchase or sale of LNG have delivery terms typically specified as either ‘delivery ex-ship’ or ‘free on board’.
Executions related to LNG portfolio-type contracts reported in Table 2 are considered reportable as LNG market data. For further information on the reporting requirements of LNG market data, see Annex III to the TRUM.
The field is mandatory when Data Field (13) Energy commodity is populated with ‘LG’.
Description of accepted values
DES = Delivery ex-ship ( ). The seller is responsible for the LNG until it is delivered to a specified port. After delivery, all obligations shift to the buyer. The delivery point is specified in the contract.
( ) DES is commonly encountered in LNG contracts, but it is no longer an official Incoterms rule. FOB = Free on board. The buyer acquires the LNG and is responsible for shipping. The delivery point may not be specified in the original contract. Both spot- and portfolio-type contracts can be agreed on an FOB basis.
OTH = Other. On rare occasions, the value ‘OTH’ may be used, for example when the delivery terms specified in the contract are different from DES or FOB.

Additional examples
1. Two market participants conclude a purchase obligation/feed-in tariffs contract with a capacity above 10 MW, i.e. regulated contracts for the physical delivery of electricity by a single production unit with a capacity greater than 10 MW or by production units with a combined capacity greater than 10 MW. In the example, the price is fixed by the provision of the relevant NRA related to the contract date.
Example of a concise representation of the formula reported in this field:
• provision NRAXX n.xxx/YYYY for offshore wind-based production;
• 13 c€/kWh in the first 10 years;
• 3 < price < 13 c€/kWh for the last five years. 2. Two market participants conclude a contract on an option for the same capacity (50 % – 50 % in volume) on the same underlying product traded at 48 EUR/MWh (the only price displayed is the forward price minus the premium, for a strike price of 47 EUR/MWh). The contract includes a clause for partial delivery meaning that the buyer has the right to take delivery for all or part of the volume. The hourly volume is requested at least two days before delivery. The charge due by the buyer is reduced by 98 % of the amount of the valuation by time period of energy not supplied on the actual day (D-Day) at the price of OMP X hourly fixing of D-Day in the case of positive prices. In the case of negative prices, the charge due by the buyer is reduced by 102 % of the amount of the valuation by time period of energy not supplied on the actual day (D-Day) at the price of the OMP X hourly fixing of D-Day.
Example of a concise representation of the formula with conditions embedded:
• if OMP X DA > 0, then (48 × energy volume – 0.98 × OMP X country A day-ahead auction hour × not delivered energy volume) / energy volume;
• else (48 × 10 – 1.02 × OMP X country A day-ahead auction hour × not delivered energy volume) / 10.
3. The formula is comprised on an index ± premium and all the other reporting conditions of Table 1 are met (e.g. a fixed volume and a fixed delivery profile). Such bilateral trade should be reported in Table 1.
Example of a concise representation of the formula of a deviation from an index (with only one index and spread):
• [name of the index] + 0.1 €/MWh.
4. Example of a concise representation of a formula defined for a period with a start date and an end date:
• 01/01/2026 – 31/03/2026: [name of the index] + 0.1 €/MWh;
• 01/04/2026 – 30/06/2026: [name of the index] + 0.5 €/MWh.
5. Example of a concise representation of a formula that varies depending on the marketplace where the transaction occurs:
• bilateral: [OTC 2023] / 5 + 0.1 €/MWh;
• exchange X: [exchange X THE 2023] / 5 + 0.15 €/MWh.
6. Example of a concise representation of a formula combining multiple conditions and time periods:
• 01/01/2026 – 31/03/2026: if [name of the index] > 30 €, then [name of the index] – 2 €; else 30 €;
• 01/04/2026 – 30/06/2026: if [name of the index] > 35 €, then [name of the index] – 4 €; else 35 €.

Notional amount
<notionalAmount> Up to 20 numerical digits in the format Number 20 53450.00 xxxx.yyyyy with a maximum of five decimals
This field identifies the notional amount of the contract. ACER understands that, in most of the cases, non-standard contracts reported in Table 2 entail features of volume and/or price flexibility and optionality, meaning that the contract is reported without a fixed price and/or quantity. In such cases, market participants shall provide an estimation (without further lifecycle reporting requirements) for the notional amount in this field, based on the best available information at the time of reporting.
The notional amount should be calculated using the following formula:
Notional amount = price × total notional contract quantity, where:
• ‘price’ is defined as the price of the volume as per Data Field (19);
• ‘total notional contract quantity’ is the quantity of energy as per Data Field (23).
For example, a contract traded for a price of 50 EUR/MWh for a volume of 100 MW delivered for 8 hours has the following notional amount:
50 EUR/MWh × 100 MW × 8 h = EUR 40 000
or, for a monthly contract:
50 EUR/MWh × 100 MW × 8 h/day × 30 days = EUR 1 200 000
For the calculation of the notional amount for options, the price reported in Data Field (45) Option strike price should be used, and not the option premium.

Annual contracted volume

This field shall be populated with the annual contracted volume, as agreed between the counterparties, representing the total amount of energy to be delivered in the next calendar year under the framework of the bilateral contract already reported in Table 2. In ACER’s understanding, annual contracted volumes are typically agreed as part of the annual delivery programmes related to LNG portfolio-type contracts (as described in Section 2.2.3), that are setting the total amount of LNG to be executed (delivered) in the following gas year.
Lifecycle reporting requirement
If applicable, the annual contracted volume reported in this field is expected to be updated each gas year with the agreed volume as a lifecycle event to the bilateral contract by using Action type M. When reporting the modification, Data Field (11) Contract date shall indicate the date of the agreement on the annual contracted volume. In addition, the dedicated schema field <reportedYear> shall be populated with the calendar year the annual contracted volume refers to.
If the terms of the reported bilateral contract do not specify any future annual contracted volumes to be agreed upon as part of the delivery schedule, the field is not applicable.

units.b: Data Field (23) Total notional contract quantity
units.t:
Total notional contract quantity
<totalNotionalContractQuantity>
Up to 20 numerical digits in the format Number 20 1000 xxxx.yyyyy with a maximum of five decimals
This field identifies the total quantity or energy volume of the contract (total notional contract quantity). Total notional contract quantity should be calculated via using the maximum defined capacity in the contract. The notional contract quantity should be calculated by using the following formula:
Total notional contract quantity = volume × number of periods, where:
• ‘volume’ is the quantity of energy as per Data Field (24) Volume optionality capacity (if available);
• ‘number of periods’ is the number of times that quantity is delivered or received as per Data Field (49).
For example, a contract traded for a volume of 100 MW delivered for 8 hours would have the following total notional contract quantity:
100 MW × 8 h = 800 MWh
or, for a monthly contract:
100 MW × 8 h × 30 days = 240 000 MWh
In case the above mentioned two elements of the formula are defined/known by the contract (especially if the volume classification of the capacity is indicated as ‘F’ for ‘fix’ in Data Field (26) Volume optionality), market participants are expected to perform the calculation of the TNCQ of the contract and report it in Data Field (23).
ACER understands that without a defined quantity, market participants will be only able to provide an estimated notional contract quantity, for example in cases where the volume optionality is indicated as ‘min/max’ in Data Field (26).
Where the total notional contract quantity is not fixed, an estimation shall be provided in this field (without further lifecycle reporting requirements). This scenario may be applicable mainly when the volume optionality is indicated as ‘complex’ or ‘variable’ in Data Field (26).
