<unit>
For fields 22 and 23: Text 2 to 8 MWh KWh MWh GWh Therm kTherm MTherm cm mcm Btu MMBtu MJ MMJ 100MJ GJ
For field 24: KW KWh/h KWh/d MW MWh/h MWh/d GW GWh/h GWh/d Therm/d KTherm/d MTherm/d cm/d mcm/d Btu/d MMBtu/d MJ/d 100MJ/d MMJ/d GJ/d
This field must identify the units used for the reported quantity in Data Field (22) Annual contracted volume, Data Field (23) Total notional contract quantity and Data Field (24) Volume optionality capacity.
Where the units for Data Fields (22), (23) and (24) differ, the different quantity units should be provided accordingly.
Data Field (26) Volume optionality 26 Volume optionality The field indicates the volume classification.
<volumeOptionality>
V = Variable Text 1 F F = Fixed M = Min/Max C = Complex O = Other
This field identifies the type of volume classification of the capacity indicated in Data Field (24). This is a representation of the flexibility of the contract capacity.
For example, it refers to the volume classification, such as variable (‘V’) (e.g. unbound variable capacity), fixed (‘F’) (e.g. 100), min/max (‘M’) (e.g. 100 to 200), complex (‘C’) (e.g. 0 [zero] or 100 to 200) or other (‘O’) (e.g. 0 or 200). For trading examples, see Annex II to the TRUM.
ACER understands that without a fixed price and/or quantity, market participants will only be able to provide an estimated notional amount. In such cases, an estimation is required and must be provided based on the best available information at the time of reporting.
‘C’ for ‘Complex’ should generally cover all cases where the volume optionality cannot be classified as one of the non-complex options (i.e. variable, fixed or min/max).
When this field is populated with ‘V’, ‘M’, ‘C’ or ‘O’, the applicable value is expected to be provided in this field.

Volume optionality frequency
<volumeOptionalityFrequency>
X = Half hourly Text 1 Q H = Hourly D = Daily W = Weekly M = Monthly Q = Quarterly S = Seasonal A = Annual O = Other
This field identifies the frequency of the volume optionality, as indicated in Data Field (26). This is a representation of how frequently the capacity of the non-standard contract can be ‘flexed’.
For example, it refers to the hourly, daily, weekly, monthly, seasonal, annual or other volume optionality frequency, as specified in the table above. It does not specify the exact dates and times when the contract capacity can be changed, but only the frequency at which the capacity can be adjusted.

Volume optionality intervals
<volumeOptionalityIntervals>
ISO 8601 date format Date n/a 2026-01-01 / 2026-03-31
This field identifies the time interval for each volume optionality, as indicated in Data Field (24), during which the market participant of the non-standard contract can adjust the volume capacity.
The field is represented by the <startDate> and <endDate> fields in the schema. If, for some reason, the <startDate> and <endDate> are not applicable (i.e. their values are not known), a dummy value ‘1900-01-01’ should be used for both fields to indicate that no volume optionality intervals are available.
Whenever Data Field (24) Volume optionality capacity must be reported, this field becomes mandatory and both Data Field (24) and Data Field (28) have to be reported within the <volumeOptionalityIntervals> element in the schema.

units.b: Data fields related to fixing index details
units.t:
Data Field (29) Type of index price 29 Type of index price The field indicates the price classified as fixed, simple index (single underlying) or complex price formula (multiple underlying).
<typeOfIndexPrice>
F = Fixed Text 1 C I = Simple Index C = Complex Price Formula O = Other
This field identifies the type of index or reference price indicated in Data Field (30) and used to set the price of the contract. Some contracts, both derivative and non-derivative, related to the delivery of gas or electricity, are traded on the basis that the price will be fixed by an index value or reference price upon its publication.
The price can be classified as:
• F = fixed; applicable when the contract has a fixed price;
• I = simple index; applicable when the price is set by a simple index (e.g. a single underlying);
• C = complex price formula; applicable when the price is set by multiple underlyings used in a formula.
The value ‘other’ may be used only in exceptional cases in which none of the above applies. In the case of ‘other’, market participants are expected to contact ACER for further guidance in order to select the appropriate type.

Fixing index
<fixingIndex>
Up to 150 alphanumerical digits Alphanumeric 150 EUGAS day-ahead publisher name This field identifies the name of the fixing index used to set the price of the transactions executed under the bilateral contract. Market participants shall report the name of the fixing index in this field. Where the contract has several fixing indices, each of them should be reported in this field.
The source of the fixing index or indices reported in this field shall be indicated in Data field (32) Fixing index sources.
Market participants shall report the name of the index as advertised by the publisher.
If the index is not public, market participants should make best efforts to minimise any discrepancy with the other market participant when reporting this information.
Further guidance on how to report bilaterally agreed index trades in Table 1 and Table 2 is available under Data Field (27) Fixing index or reference price in Table 1.
Only indices related to an energy commodity should be reported in this field. This would also include oil and coal, or any other energy commodity to fix the price of gas or electricity. This implies that there is no need to report foreign-exchange reference in the fixing index details section of Table 2. If, for any reason, market participants want to report foreign-exchange reference, it can be reported in the formula under Data Field (19) Price or price formula.

Fixing index types
<fixingIndexType>
SO = Spot Text Up to 5 FW FW = Forward style contract FU = Future style contract OP = Option style contract OP_FW = Option on a forward OP_FU = Option on a future OP_SW = Option on a swap SP = Spread SW = Swap OT = Other
This field identifies the type of fixing index indicated in Data Field (30) and used in the bilateral contract that is being reported. Where the contract has several types of fixing indices, each of them should be reported in this field.
For example, if the index is a spot price published by an exchange, the value ‘SO’ shall be reported. If the index is published by a price-reporting agency or other publisher and it represents the delivery of the energy commodity during a specific day, week, weekend, month, etc., the value ‘FW’ shall be reported. If the index is a future price published by an exchange, the value ‘FU’ shall be reported.
In the case of ‘other’, market participants are expected to contact ACER for further guidance in order to select the appropriate index type.

Fixing index sources
<fixingIndexSource>
Up to 150 alphanumerical digits Alphanumeric 100 Index source name
This field identifies the source of the fixing index or indices reported in Data Field (30) Fixing index. Where the bilateral contracts have several sources for the fixing indices, each source should be reported in this field.
For each index reported in Data Field (30), market participants shall specify the publication source of the index. In the case of a basket of indices for which no unique publisher exists, market participants shall report all sources of the basket of indices.
For example, if the index ‘EU-GAS-CALENDAR-YEAR-2015-PUB-NAME’ is reported in Data Field (30), market participants shall report the source of the index publication, for example ‘EU-GAS-PRICES-PUB-NAME’, and the publisher’s name, for example ‘PUB-NAME’, needed to identify where the index is published. This applies to each individual index reported in Data Field (31).
If the indices ‘EU-GAS-CALENDAR-YEAR-2015-PUB-NAME-ABC’ and ‘EU-GAS-CALENDAR-YEAR-2015-PUB-NAME-123’ are reported in Data Field (30), market participants shall report the source of the publication for both, for example ‘PUB-NAME-ABC’ and PUB-NAME-123’.

First fixing date
<firstFixingDate> ISO 8601 date format Date n/a 2026-01-29
This field identifies the first date at which the price of the bilateral contracts can be set using the index indicated in Data Field (30) Fixing index.
If the bilateral contract has several indices and each of them may be used to set the price of the contract or the executions, market participants shall report the first date at which the price can be fixed for each index reported in Data Field (30).
For example: 1. the index ABC may be used to fix the price from 2026-01-01 to 2027-12-31; 2. the index 123 may be used to fix the price from 2026-08-01 to 2028-03-31; and 3. the index XYZ may be used to fix the price from 2026-12-01 to 2029-03-31.
In this case, market participants shall report ‘2026-01-01’, ‘2026-08-01’ and ‘2026-12-01’ in this field.

Last fixing date
<lastFixingDate>
ISO 8601 date format Date n/a 2034-01-29
This field identifies the last date at which the price of the contract can be fixed using the index indicated in Data Field (30) Fixing index.
If the contract has several indices and each of them may be used to set the price of the contract or the executions, market participants shall report the last date at which the price can be fixed for each index reported in Data Field (30).
For example: 1. the index ABC may be used to fix the price from 2026-01-01 to 2027-12-31; 2. the index 123 may be used to fix the price from 2026-04-01 to 2028-03-31; and 3. the index XYZ may be used to fix the price from 2026-04-01 to 2029-03-31.
In this case, ‘2027-12-31’, ‘2028-03-31’ and ‘2029-03-31’ shall be reported in this field.
If the last fixing date is equal to Data Field (33) First fixing date, the field should not be reported.

Fixing frequency
<fixingFrequency>
X = Half hourly Text 1 W H = Hourly D = Daily W = Weekly M = Monthly Q = Quarterly S = Seasonal A = Annual O = Other
This field identifies the frequency of the fixing of the index reported in Data Field (30).
For example, it refers to the daily, weekly, monthly, seasonal, annual or other frequency, as specified in the table above. The information reported in this field does not specify the exact dates and times when the fixing occurs, but only its frequency.
The price of the contract or the executions can be set on the basis of an index that is used daily or monthly.
In the case of ‘other’, market participants are expected to contact ACER for further guidance in order to select the appropriate frequency type.

Settlement method
<settlementMethod> P = Physically settled without optionality Text 1 P
C = Cash settled without optionality 1
P_OP = Physically settled with optionality 4
C_OP = Cash settled with optionality 4
This field identifies the type of settlement for the bilateral contract.
The majority of bilateral contracts traded under REMIT are for physical delivery, but there may also be derivative contracts that are not reported under EMIR and are thus reported under REMIT. Consequently, different types of settlement methods may apply. For bilateral contracts, such as options on futures or swaps, which settle into the underlying future or swap, the settlement method should be considered to be physical delivery of the underlying contract, and the value ‘P’ should be reported.
Description of accepted values
P = physically settled without optionality. ‘P’ shall be reported for contracts that are settled physically (typical for spot/physical forwards). The field shall also be populated with ‘P’ in the case of derivative contracts relating to a wholesale energy product that must be physically settled. For contracts such as options on forwards/futures/swaps, the option settles into the underlying forward/future/swap. Since the underlying contract is considered for physical delivery, the value ‘P’ shall be reported.
C = cash settled without optionality. ‘C’ shall be reported for contracts that are settled in cash without an optionality, i.e. must be settled in cash.
P_OP = physically settled with optionality. ‘P_OP’ shall be reported for contracts that are physically settled while the market participant had an optionality over the settlement method.
C_OP = cash settled with optionality. ‘C_OP’ shall be reported for contracts that are settled in cash while the market participant had an optionality over the settlement method.

Option style
<optionStyle> A = American Text 1 B B = Bermudan E = European S = Asian O = Other
This field identifies the option style, usually defined by the dates on which the option may be exercised: American, European, Bermudan, Asian or other.
An American-style option can be exercised at any time during its life, both prior to and on its maturity date. A European-style option can only be exercised on its maturity date. A Bermudan-style option can only be exercised on specified dates indicated in the bilateral contract.
Market participants should refer to financial markets to identify the option style they are reporting. Exotic option styles, such as binary, barrier, window options, etc., should be reported with the value ‘O’.
In the case of ‘other’, market participants are expected to contact ACER for further guidance in order to select the most appropriate option style.

Option type
<optionType>
P = Put Text 1 C C = Call O = Other
This field identifies the type of right that the option holder owns, which may be a call option or a put option. ‘C’ shall be indicated if the option is a call option, and ‘P’ shall be indicated if the option is a put option. If the option holder owns a type of right different from a put or a call, the value ‘O’ for ‘other’ shall be reported in this field.
In the case of ‘other’, market participants are expected to contact ACER for further guidance in order to select the appropriate option type.
Reporting parties should refer to financial markets to identify the option type they are reporting.

units.b: Data Field (39) Option first exercise date
units.t:
Option first exercise date
<optionFirstExerciseDate>
ISO 8601 date format Date n/a 2026-01-29
This field identifies the first date at which the option holder has the right, but not the obligation, to buy or sell the commodity or the underlying instrument at a specified price using the index indicated in Data Field (42) Option strike index or the price reported in Data Field (45) Option strike price.
For example, the counterparty to the bilateral contract that holds the option may exercise, against the option strike index indicated in Data Field (42), the right to buy or sell the energy commodity from 01/01/2026 to 31/12/2028 (on specific dates or at specific intervals), in which case the market participant shall report ‘01/01/2026’ in this field.
Where the bilateral contract has several indices and where each of them may be used to exercise the right to buy or sell the energy commodity, market participants shall report the first date at which the option can be exercised per each index reported in Data Field (42). For example:
1. the index ABC may be used to exercise the option from 2026-01-01 to 2027-12-31; 2. the index 123 may be used to exercise the option from 2027-04-01 to 2028-03-31; and 3. the index XYZ may be used to exercise the option from 2028-04-01 to 2029-03-31.
In this case, ‘2026-01-01’, ‘2027-04-01’ and ‘2028-04-01’ shall be reported in this field for examples 1–3, respectively.

units.b: Data Field (40) Option last exercise date
units.t:
Option last exercise date
<optionLastExerciseDate>
ISO 8601 date format Date n/a 2027-01-29 This field identifies the last date at which the option holder has the right, but not the obligation, to buy or sell the commodity or underlying instrument at a specified price using the index indicated in Data Field (42) Option strike index or the price reported in Data Field (45) Option strike price.
For example, the counterparty to the bilateral contract that holds the option may exercise, against the option strike index indicated in Data Field (42), the right to buy or sell the energy commodity from 01/01/2026 to 31/12/2028 (on specific dates or at specific intervals), in which case the market participant shall report ‘31/12/2028’ in this field.
Where the bilateral contract has several indices and where each of them may be used to exercise the right to buy or sell the energy commodity, market participants shall report the last date at which the option can be exercised per each index reported in Data Field (42). For example:
1. the index ABC may be used to exercise the option from 2026-01-01 to 2027-12-31; 2. the index 123 may be used to exercise the option from 2026-04-01 to 2028-03-31; and 3. the index XYZ may be used to exercise the option from 2026-04-01 to 2029-03-31.
In this case, ‘2027-12-31’, ‘2028-03-31’ and ‘2029-03-31’ shall be reported in this field for examples 1– 3, respectively.

Option exercise frequency
<optionExerciseFrequency>
D = Daily Text 1 W W = Weekly M = Monthly S = Seasonal A = Annual O = Other
This field identifies the frequency at which the option holder has the right, but not the obligation, to buy or sell the commodity or underlying instrument at a specified price using the index indicated in Data Field (42) Option strike index or the price reported in Data Field (45) Option strike price.
For example, a counterparty to the bilateral contract that holds the option may exercise, against the option strike index indicated in Data Field (42), the right to buy or sell the energy commodity on a monthly basis, in which case the market participant shall report ‘M’ in this field. The same applies to the other types of frequencies. Where the bilateral contract has several indices and where each of them may be used to exercise the right to buy or sell the energy commodity, market participants shall report the frequency at which the option can be exercised per each index reported in Data Field (42). For example:
1. the index ABC may be used to exercise the option from 2025-01-01 to 2027-12-31 on a daily basis; 2. the index 123 may be used to exercise the option from 2026-04-01 to 2028-03-31on a monthly basis; and 3. the index XYZ may be used to exercise the option from 2012-04-01 to 2029-03-31 on a weekly basis.
In this case, ‘D’, ‘M’ and ‘W’ shall be reported in this field for examples 1–3, respectively.
In the case of ‘Other’, market participants are expected to contact ACER for further guidance in order to select the appropriate frequency type.

Option strike index
<optionStrikeIndex>
Up to 150 alphanumerical digits Alphanumeric 150 Index name
This field identifies the name of the strike index used in the index option embedded in the bilateral contract. Market participants shall report the name of the index in this field.
An index option is a call or put option contract in which the underlying asset is an index of any sort. For example, in a call, a market participant may buy the right to an index on or before the expiration date at a certain strike index.
Some options, both derivative and non-derivative, related to physical delivery of gas or electricity are traded on the basis that the option may be exercised against an index or reference price upon its publication.
Market participants shall report the name of the index as advertised by the publisher.
If the index is not public, market participants should make best efforts to minimise any discrepancy with the other market participant when reporting this information.
Market participants may consider using the following convention:
[commodity]-[delivery area]-[delivery period]-[index name]-[publisher name] For example:
1. GAS-DAYAHEAD-INDEX-PUBLISHERNAME; 2. GAS-EU-FRONTMONTH-AVERAGEPRICE-PUBLISHERNAME; 3. ELECTRICITY-COUNTRY A-FRONTMONTH-FUTURE-EXCHANGENAME.

units.b: Data Field (43) Option strike index type
units.t:
Option strike index type
<optionIndexType>
SO = Spot Text 2 FW FW = Forward style contract FU = Future style contract OP = Option style contract OP_FW = Option on a forward OP_FU = Option on a future OP_SW = Option on a swap SP = Spread SW = Swap OT = Other
This field identifies the type of strike index of the option used in the bilateral contract, as reported in Data Field (42). For each index, market participants shall specify the type of index.
For example, if the index is a spot price published by an exchange, the value ‘SO’ shall be reported.
If the index is published by a price-reporting agency or other publisher and it represents the delivery of the energy commodity during a specific day, week, weekend, month, etc., the value ‘FW’ shall be reported. If the index is a future price published by an exchange, the value ‘FU’ shall be reported.
Where the bilateral contract has several indices and where each of them may be used to exercise the right to buy or sell the energy commodity, market participants shall report the type of index used against which the option can be exercised per each index reported in Data Field (42) Option strike index. For example:
1. the spot price published by exchange ABC may be used to exercise the option from 2026-01-01 to 2027-12-31; 2. the index value for a forward contract published by publisher 123 may be used to exercise the option from 2026-04-01 to 2028-03-31; and 3. the future price published by exchange XYZ may be used to exercise the option from 2026-04-01 to 2029-03-31. In this case, ‘SO’, ‘FW’ and ‘FU’ shall be reported in this field for examples 1–3, respectively.
In the case of ‘other’, market participants are expected to contact ACER for further guidance in order to select the appropriate index type.

units.b: Data Field (44) Option strike index source
units.t:
Option strike index source
<optionIndexSource>
Up to 150 alphanumerical digits Alphanumeric 100 Index source name
This field identifies the source of strike index of the option used in the bilateral contract, as reported in Data Field (42) Option strike index. For each index, market participants shall specify the source of the index.
For example, if the index is a spot price published by exchange ABC, the name of the exchange shall be reported. If the index is published by a price-reporting agency or other publisher, the name of the publisher shall be reported.
Where the bilateral contract has several indices and where each of them may be used to exercise the option, market participants shall report the source of each index reported in Data Field (42) Option strike index against which the option can be exercised. For example:
1. the spot price published daily by the exchange ABC may be used to exercise the option from 2026-01-01 to 2027-12-31; 2. the index value for a forward contract published by publisher 123 may be used to exercise the option from 2026-04-01 to 2028-03-31; and 3. the future price published by the exchange XYZ may be used to exercise the option from 2026-04-01 to 2029-03-31.
In this case, ‘exchange ABC’, ‘publisher 123’ and ‘exchange XYZ’ shall be reported in this field for examples 1–3, respectively.

Option strike price
<optionStrikePrice>
Up to 20 numerical digits in the Number 20 125.98 format xxxxx.yyyyy with a maximum of five decimals
This field identifies the price at which the owner of the option can buy (in the case of a call option) or sell (in the case of a put option) the energy commodity (gas or electricity) or the instrument, as indicated in the option contract, for example future/forward/swap.
This field shall be reported only if the strike price is available. In the case of an option strike index where the strike price is not available, this field is not applicable.
Where the option has several strike prices and where each of them may be used to exercise the right to buy or sell the energy commodity, market participants shall report all the strike prices at which the option can be exercised.

units.b: Data Field (46) Delivery point or zone
units.t:
Delivery point or zone
<deliveryPointOrZone>
EIC code, 16-character Alphanumeric 16 10YCB-EUROPEU–8 alphanumeric code
This field should indicate the EIC Y, Z or W code to identify the delivery point or zone for the bilateral contract.
Any bilateral contract related to the supply of electricity or gas, irrespective of whether it is a spot, a physical forward, a future or an option contract, has a reference to a delivery point or zone. Also, financial derivatives related to EU electricity or gas have a reference price or other attributes that relate to the delivery of the commodity.
For more information, see Section 2.3.

Delivery start date
<deliveryStartDateTime>
ISO 8601 date format Date n/a 2026-01-01
This field identifies the start date of delivery of the commodity under the reported bilateral contract.
Data Fields (46) and (47), for delivery start date and delivery end date, respectively, are mandatory fields. However, ACER is aware of the fact that, given the characteristics of some bilateral contracts reported in Table 2, it is not always possible to report both fields when reporting the contract in Table 2. If the delivery start date is unknown, by default, ‘1900-01-01’ should be reported in this field.

Delivery end date
<deliveryEndDateTime>
ISO 8601 date format Date n/a 2027-01-31
This field identifies the end date of delivery of the commodity under the reported bilateral contract.
Data Fields (46) and (47), for delivery start date and delivery end date, respectively, are mandatory fields. However, ACER is aware of the fact that, given the characteristics of some bilateral contracts reported in Table 2, it is not always possible to report both fields when reporting the contract in Table 2. If the delivery end date is unknown, by default, ‘2100-12-31’ should be reported in this field.

Number of periods
<numberOfPeriod>
Up to 20 numerical digits in the format Number 20 120 xxxxx.yyyyy with a maximum of five decimals
This field represents the calculated number of time units over which the quantity is delivered, based on the delivery profile and using an hourly resolution. It reflects the total count of distinct hourly periods over which deliveries occur within the bilateral contract’s time frame.
Market participants should derive this value directly from the delivery schedule, ensuring that it aligns with the reported delivery start and end dates and the specified load type. The calculation should account for all applicable hours in which delivery occurs.
For example, under a baseload (‘BL’) contract starting on 1 January at 00:00:00 and ending on 6 January at 00:00:00, the number of hourly periods would be calculated as 5 days × 24 hours = 120 periods. The value to be reported in this field is therefore ‘120’.
Bilateral contract with non-continuous deliveries (e.g. peak-load (‘PL’), off-peak-load (‘OP’), shaped (‘SH’)) shall only include the periods corresponding to the specific delivery profile.
This field is only applicable to non-standard contracts with a fixed delivery profile. If the delivery profile is not fixed, there is no expectation to provide the number of periods in this data field, or to provide an estimation.

Load type
<loadType> BL = Baseload Text 2 BL PL = Peak-load OP = Off-Peak load BH = Hour/Block Hours SH = Shaped GD = Gas-Day OT = Other
This field identifies the delivery profile (baseload, peak-load, off-peak-load, block of hours or other) of the bilateral contract. The load type should be identified as defined in the bilateral contract, if available.
BL = Baseload. The contracted volume to supply electricity is delivered continuously for all 24 hours of the day. PL = Peak-load. The product is delivered only during the peak-demand hours of the day, rather than continuously like in a baseload contract. Peak hours may vary by Member State, but a common definition in many European power markets is from Monday to Friday, starting from 07:00 or 08:00 until 19:00 or 20:00, respectively (excluding weekends and holidays).
OP = Off-peak-load. The product is delivered during all the hours outside the defined peak-load period. Off-peak hours depend on the market, but a common definition in many European power markets is from Monday to Friday, starting from 19:00 or 20:00 until 07:00 or 08:00, respectively, including weekends and holidays.
BH = Hour/Block Hours. The product is delivered in a predefined set of hours each day (fixed hourly blocks), distinguishing it from baseload, peak-load or off-peak-load delivery profiles.
SH = Shaped. A contract that is considered to have a customised delivery profile, i.e. it specifies the amount of energy to be bought or sold at different points in time in order to allow the market participant to meet their specific needs.
GD = Gas-day. Natural gas is delivered continuously during the day, typically from 06:00 to 06:00 the next day. For within-day contracts where the delivery of the gas is running from a certain hour of the gas day until 06:00 the next day, load type ‘GD’ is considered applicable.
OT = Other. If a delivery profile is not defined, market participants shall report ‘OT’ for ‘Other’. In the case of value ‘OT’, market participants are expected to contact ACER for further guidance in order to select the appropriate delivery profile type.
For the application of the correct load type for a specific product or contract, see the examples available in Annex II to the TRUM.

units.b: Data field related to lifecycle information
units.t:
Data Field (51) Action type
• a modification of details of a previously reported bilateral contract, it will be identified as ‘modify’;
• a cancellation of a wrongly reported bilateral contract, it will be identified as ‘error’;
• a termination of an outstanding bilateral contract, it will be identified as ‘cancel’.
<actionType>
N = New Text 1 N M = Modify E = Error C = Cancel
This field identifies the type of action representing a lifecycle event that occurred in relation to the bilateral contract that is being reported.
The requirements for reporting lifecycle events related to transactions reportable in Table 1 and Table 2 are described in detail in Annex I to the TRUM.
The field is mandatory for all bilateral contracts reported in Table 2.
Description of the accepted values
Action type N (‘new’) always indicates the first event in any transaction’s lifecycle. This implies that the first contract record shall always be reported with Action type N. A subsequent record with Action type M, C or E can be accepted by ARIS only if a record with Action type N has been successfully reported previously. The first submission of a non-standard contract is an event that will be identified as ‘new’.
Action type M (‘modify’) shall be adopted in case there is a modification of the previously submitted record, which is triggered by a business decision or is the result of a business event. An example of a report modification is when two parties agree to amend one or more terms of the original agreement (e.g. price, quantity or any other value previously reported).
Action type C (‘cancel’) indicates the last event in the lifecycle sequence, triggered by a business decision or resulting from a business event. For example, at any time during the term of a contract, the counterparties may agree to terminate the contract early (i.e. before its natural maturity date).
Action type E (‘error’) shall be used if the reporting party needs to indicate that the previously submitted record was erroneously reported, meaning that it was incorrect. Any correction to the already reported information using Action type E will result in a logical deletion (i.e. invalidation) of the corresponding record, which was previously successfully reported. It will, however, not delete the previously reported record from the ARIS database. Reporting an event with Action type E cannot be the result of a business decision, for example to change the economic values, such as price or quantity.
For further information on the application of the different action types, see Annex I to the TRUM.
fn: 51 Action type When the report refers to: • a bilateral contract reported for the first time, it will be identified as ‘new’;

units.b: Data fields related to electricity transportation contracts to be reported in Table 3
units.t:
Technical and business requirements when submitting the transaction record
In this chapter, ACER provides information on how the data fields listed in Table 3 of the Annex to the REMIT Implementing Regulation shall be populated for the reporting of both standard and non-standard electricity transportation contracts.
It is worth noting that not all data fields are mandatory for all transactions. Data fields are expected to be populated when applicable, according to this manual. ACER has prepared a list of trading scenarios to show what is expected and applicable to each scenario. The trading scenarios are listed in Annex II to the TRUM.

Document identification
<mRID>
Sender unique identification String Maximum 35 A_R-IT-FR-I-HOURLY1624-140709-01
This field indicates the unique identification of the document for which the time series data is being supplied. A bid document for a given time series set and a given bid period must have a unique identification assigned by the sender of the document for all transmissions to the receiver.
All additions, modifications or suppressions for the time series and bid period must use the same identification.
This field is always mandatory.

Document version
<revisionNumber>
An integer value starting with 1. Integer Maximum 3 1 1 2 3 … 999
This field identifies the document version. The document version is used to identify a given version of a time series set for a given bid period. The first version number for a given document identification shall normally be 1. The document version number must be incremented for each retransmission of a document that contains changes to the previous version. The version number shall always be greater than the previous version number of the same document.
Data Field (2) plays an important role when the document has to be deleted. More specifically, in order to delete incorrect bids or total allocation reports, Data Field (2) Document version has to be updated, as described above. To withdraw these documents, a higher version of the relevant document, containing only a header and no TimeSeries, should be sent.
This field is always mandatory.

units.t:
Offered capacity
<offeredCapacity_Quantity.quantity>
The maximum length of this Numeric Maximum 10.8 information is 17 numeric characters 17 (decimal mark included).
This field shall identify the total capacity offered by the relevant TSO at the auction, as identified in Data Field (19) Auction identification.
In general, for monthly and yearly auctions, the offered capacity is understood as the sum of the available transmission capacity (ATC) and the capacity returned to the auction. For an initial yearly auction, there is no preceding long-term allocation time frame from which capacity can be returned, but returned capacity may be available in subsequent yearly auction rounds and included in the offered capacity.
For explicit day-ahead auctions, the offered capacity and ATC are equal.
The capacity reported in Data Field (32) shall not include the capacity that was returned to the auction from the secondary market. The return capacity is to be indicated in Data Field (34).
The field is to be populated by the OMP reporting the auction with the applicable offered capacity.
The offered capacity shall always be expressed in MW. The number of decimal places identifying the fractional part of the quantity depends on local market rules.
The field is mandatory for primary allocations.

Available transmission capacity
<transCapacity_Quantity.quantity>
The maximum length of this Numeric Maximum 10.8 information is 17 numeric characters 17 (decimal mark included).
This field shall identify the ATC available at the auction, as identified in Data Field (19) Auction identification.
The field is to be populated by the OMP reporting the auction with the applicable ATC.
The ATC value shall always be expressed in MW. The number of decimal places identifying the fractional part of the quantity depends on local market rules.
The field is mandatory for primary allocations.

Return capacity
< returnCapacity_Quantity.quantity>
The maximum length of this Numeric Maximum 10.8 information is 17 numeric characters 17 (decimal mark included).
This field shall identify the total capacity returned to the auction, as identified in Data Field (19) Auction identification.
The field is to be populated by the OMP reporting the auction where the capacity was returned. In the section AuctionSpecificationData in the electronic format, the ID of the auction where the capacity was originally allocated shall be reported, together with the information on the capacity that has been returned to the auction, as identified in Data Field (19). In addition, the ID of the market participant returning the capacity to the auction (as identified in Data Field (19)) is also expected to be reported.
The return capacity shall always be expressed in MW. The number of decimal places identifying the fractional part of the quantity depends on local market rules.
The field is mandatory for primary allocations when the auction offers capacity that was previously returned from the secondary allocation to the auction.

<businessType>
Refer to the ENTSO-E code list for Alphanumeric 3 A57 data interchange document for the valid list codes. A32 = Capacity transfer notification
A57 = Resale pricing

It is important to distinguish between returns and transfers.
Code ‘A32’ refers to the notification of the transfer of capacity to another market participant. Transfer is considered applicable when one market participant transfers the capacity allocated to them previously via the primary allocation to another market participant on the secondary market. Therefore, this code shall be used in the case of secondary allocations.
Code ‘A57’ refers to the resold capacity and is expected to be used when the market participant that acquired capacity previously via a primary allocation returns the capacity back to another auction.
This field is mandatory.

Time interval
<Period> <timeInterval> <start>
<Period> <timeInterval> <end>
ISO 8601 date format using UTC Date and time 41 2026-03-01T13:00Z/2027-05-11T15:30Z
This field identifies the start and end date and time of the period in question. The start and end time is expressed in UTC.
There may be several period classes for a time series. The overall time interval covered by the period shall be within the complete rights time interval. The number of periods within a time series, as characterised by the resolution, must completely cover the period’s time interval. If a time series is suppressed, the interval quantities are all zeroed out.
This field is mandatory.

Resolution
<Period> <resolution>
The resolution is expressed in Date and time PnYnMnDTnHnMnS PT15M compliance with ISO 8601. For example, PT15M expresses a 15-minute resolution.
This field identifies the number of periods that the time interval is divided into, where ‘nY’ expresses the number of years, ‘nM’ the number of months and ‘nD’ the number of days. The letter ‘T’ separates the date expression from the time expression and, after it, ‘nH’ identifies the number of hours, ‘nM’ the number of minutes and ‘nS’ the number of seconds.
This information defines the resolution of a single period. The time interval must contain a whole number of periods, as expressed by the resolution.
This field is mandatory.

Position
<Period> <Point> <position>
The relative position must be Integer Maximum 6 1 expressed as a numeric integer value beginning with 1. All leading zeros must be suppressed. The maximum number of characters is 6. 1 2 3 … 999999
This field provides the relative position of a period within an interval.
This field is mandatory, if available.

Quantity
<Period> <Point> <quantity>
The maximum length of this Numeric Maximum 17 10.8 information is 17 numeric characters (decimal mark included).
This field defines the quantity that has been assigned to the nomination party for the interval in question and that is expressed in the measurement unit. A decimal point value may be used to express values that are inferior to the defined unit of measurement. The decimal mark that separates the digits forming the integral part of a number from those forming the fractional part (ISO 6093) shall always be a period (‘.’). All quantities are non-signed values.
In the case of unmatched bids (‘unsuccessful bids’) that do not result in a transaction and thus in allocated capacity, this field should be populated with ‘0’ (zero).
The number of decimal places identifying the fractional part of the quantity depends on local market rules.

<Period> <Point> <price.amount>
The maximum length of this Numeric Maximum 17 1.8 information is 17 numeric characters ISO 6093 (decimal mark and sign included, if used).
This field indicates the price expressed for each unit, i.e. the price indicated in a resale document equal to or above which the quantity may be sold.
This information defines the price, expressed as price per unit of quantity, in compliance with the pricing scheme based on local market rules. The decimal mark that separates the digits forming the integral part of a number from those forming the fractional part (ISO 6093) shall always be a period (‘.’).
This field is mandatory, if available.

<Reason> <code>
Refer to the ENTSO-E code list for Alphanumeric Maximum 3 A75 data interchange document for the valid list of codes. A75 = Rights status information A71 = Linked bid rejected due to associated bid unsuccessful
A72 = Original bid divided to permit acceptance

Subject party
<Subject_MarketParticipant> <mRID>
EIC Alphanumeric 16 10X1001A1001A450
This field identifies the party that is the capacity trader for whom the bids are being submitted. The codification scheme used for the coded identification is indicated by the coding scheme attribute.
This field is mandatory.

Subject role
<Subject_MarketParticipant> <marketRole.type>
Refer to the ENTSO-E code list for data Alphanumeric Maximum 3 A29 interchange document for the valid list of codes. A29 = Capacity trader
This field identifies the role of the subject party. In this current implementation of ECAN (Capacity Allocation and Nomination System), the role shall always be ‘A29’ (capacity trader).

Divisible
<divisible>
A01 = Yes Alphanumeric Maximum 3 A01
A02 = No
This field indicates whether each element of the bid may be marginal. This means that the quantity allocated to each element of the bid may be any value between 0 and the quantity asked. If it is not divisible, the quantity may be either 0 or the quantity. This is only applicable to the last assessed bid. In the case of capacity auctions, if the ATC limit is reached, ‘divisible’ means that it may be reduced to the ATC limit and partially accepted.
This field is mandatory, if available.

This field identifies a set of bids that are linked together, signifying that they are either all accepted or all rejected. This identification is defined by the bidder and must be unique for a given auction. The linked bid identification is only provided if another bid is associated with the current bid. units.b: Data fields related to natural gas transportation contracts to be reported in Table 4
units.t:
Technical and business requirements when submitting the transaction record
This chapter sets out the reporting requirements for reporting parties on how to populate the data fields included in Table 4 of the Annex to the REMIT Implementing Regulation when reporting transactions relating to wholesale energy products associated with the transportation of natural gas in the EU, pursuant to Article 3(b) of the REMIT Implementing Regulation. Table 4 shall be used for the reporting of transactions referring to both standard and non-standard gas transportation contracts.
The data fields included in Table 4 are expected to be populated according to the cardinality table below and the reporting requirements explained under the individual data fields. In addition, for further clarification, a non-exhaustive list of trading scenarios is available in Annex II to the TRUM.
In accordance with Article 13(4) of the REMIT Implementing Regulation, ACER has established the electronic formats for reporting transactions related to gas transportation contracts based on established industry standards by adopting for Table 4 the standard set out by Edig@s.

units.t:
Sender identification
<issuer_MarketParticipant.identification>
ACER code Alphanumeric 12 A0643278W.EU
This field indicates the ACER registration code of the RRM sending the document.
The Edig@s message includes ‘standard header information’ and requires the indication of the coding scheme attribute. For ACER codes, it shall be equal to ‘ACE’.
Both the identification and the coding scheme are mandatory for primary and secondary allocations.

No. | Field Identifier | Description
Organised marketplace identification
<organisedMarketPlace_MarketParticipant.identification>
ACER code Alphanumeric 12 A0643278W.EU 10X1001A1001A450 EIC X 16 This field identifies the OMP where the capacity was offered. This can be a booking platform ( ) or an individual TSO platform.
If the allocation was executed on an OMP, this field must contain the ACER code, as reported in the ‘List of organised marketplaces’ published by ACER, or an EIC X-type code. For ACER codes, the coding scheme attribute shall be equal to ‘ACE’, while for EIC X-type codes it shall be equal to ‘305’.
Where the allocation procedure does not take place on an OMP (i.e. bilateral secondary allocation), this field shall be populated with the default value ‘21X-XXXXXXXXXXXY’.
Both the identification and the coding scheme are mandatory for primary and secondary allocations.

Process identification
<process_Transaction.identification>
Up to 35 alphanumerical digits Alphanumeric Up to 35 590825
This field identifies the specific capacity auction by a unique code.
The value reported for the population of this field shall match the relevant auction code, as indicated in any public information issued by the OMP.
Primary allocations
In the case of primary allocations, the code is uniquely assigned by the OMP that hosts the capacity allocation. The process identification shall be unique within a particular OMP, but the same code can also be used by other OMPs.
Secondary allocations
As indicated for primary allocations, the same applies in the case of secondary allocations occurring on an OMP. The field is also considered mandatory for bilateral secondary allocations (i.e. when the capacity has been allocated bilaterally outside of an OMP), such as shipper–shipper transactions. In such cases, the field shall be populated with the unique identification code of the allocation, as agreed bilaterally by the counterparties.
( ) As defined in Commission Regulation (EU) 2017/459 of 16 March 2017 establishing a network code on capacity allocation mechanisms in gas transmission systems and repealing Regulation (EU) No 984/2013. For bilateral transactions reported with values ‘OTC’ or ‘OTC_SUB’ (‘A03’ or ‘A06’, respectively) in Data Field (33) Procedure applicable, this field shall be populated with the default value ‘OTC’. In all other cases, the actual process ID would be required.

Type of gas
<process_Transaction.taxonomy.energyProductType>
HC1 = High calorific Alphanumeric 3 HC1
LC1 = Low calorific
This field identifies the type of gas that the capacity allocation refers to. The value ‘HC1’ shall be populated for high calorific value gas, and ‘LC1’ for low calorific value gas.
The field is mandatory for allocations occurring via auctions.

Transportation transaction identification
<Transportation_Transaction> <identification>
Up to 35 digits Alphanumeric Up to 35 111-67A4552
This field indicates the unique identification code of the transportation transaction.
The field is mandatory for primary and secondary allocations.
Primary allocations For primary allocations, the value reported in this field shall provide a unique code that clearly identifies the primary capacity allocation, as assigned by the transmission capacity allocator (e.g. the OMP).
In the case of a successful transaction (i.e. successful bid) that results in capacity being allocated to a market participant, the unique code that identifies the capacity allocation shall correspond to the identifier of the concluded transaction between the TSO and the ‘successful market participant’.
In the case of an unsuccessful bid that does not result in allocated capacity, a unique code is still assigned by the transmission capacity allocator with the aim of identifying the bidding behaviour of the relevant market participant that submitted the unsuccessful bid (such a market participant may be referred to as an ‘unsuccessful market participant’) during the allocation process.
It is ACER’s understanding that the TSO may generate the transportation transaction identification (for both successful and unsuccessful market participants) as follows:
Process identification reported in Data Field (3), followed by ‘-‘ (dash), followed by the EIC code of the relevant network user.
Secondary allocations
For secondary allocations, the value reported in this field provides a uniquely assigned identification number for the allocation made between the transferor and the transferee, as assigned by the transmission capacity allocator or as agreed between the balancing group(s) or shipper(s) for bilaterally agreed capacity allocations. The value reported in this field by the transferor shall thus be equal to the one reported by the transferee.

units.b: Data Field (6) Creation date and time
units.t:
Creation date and time
<process_Transaction.transaction_DateTime.dateTime>
ISO 8601 date and time format using Date and time Up to 30 2026-01-29T10:35:56Z UTC
This field indicates the date and time of the execution of the transaction, i.e. the transaction timestamp. The field must reflect the actual time as accurately as possible, reported as a string representation of the ISO 8601 date and time format. The timestamp shall always be represented in UTC, thus expressed either in Zulu time, or in local time with the time zone offset indicated.
This field is mandatory for primary and secondary allocations.
Primary allocation If the allocation occurs via an auction, this field shall reflect the time of the announcement of the auction results or any subsequent modifications or cancellations of the transaction. However, ACER is aware that reporting parties may sometimes not be in a position to know the exact time of the announcement of the auction results. In such cases, this field can be populated with the gate closure time of the auction. The same applies to auctions where bids were submitted by market participants bidding for the offered capacity, but no allocation took place.
Data Field (6) Creation date and time corresponds to the attribute <process_Transaction.transaction_DateTime.dateTime> in the Edig@s schema. In the schema, there is also the element <creationDateTime> available, which reflects the date and time at which the electronic report file was created but shall not be used to report the transaction timestamp specified in this field. With regard to the date and time information mentioned above, ACER understands that there may be a delay between the execution time of the transaction and the time of the xml file creation.
Secondary allocation
For secondary allocations, this field shall indicate the date and time when the two counterparties agreed on the conclusion of the transaction. The timestamp shall be rounded to the nearest minute in the UTC format (e.g. 2026-01-29T10:35Z).

units.b: Data Field (7) Auction open date and time
units.t:
Auction open date and time
<process_Transaction.auctionOpen_DateTime.dateTime>
ISO 8601 date and time format using Date and time Up to 30 2026-01-29T10:35:56Z UTC
This field indicates the date and time when the auction opened for bidding. Auction open date and time shall be expressed in the ISO 8601 date format using UTC.
The field is mandatory if the primary or secondary allocation occurs via an auction but not applicable if the allocation process does not involve an auction or a call for orders.
Data Field (8) Auction end date and time <process_Transaction.auctionEnd_DateTime.dateTime>
ISO 8601 date and time format using Date and time Up to 30 2026-01-29T10:35:56Z UTC
This field indicates the date and time when the auction closes for bidding, i.e. the gate closure. The auction end date and time shall always refer to the last point in time when a market participant can submit bids and when trading can occur. Auction end date and time are expressed in the ISO 8601 date format using UTC.
The field is mandatory for primary and secondary allocations occurring via auctions.
If the allocation process does not involve an auction (e.g. secondary allocations occurring outside an OMP) or a call for orders, this field is not applicable.
fn: 8 Auction end date and time The field indicates the date and time when an auction closes.

units.t:

ZEL = Monthly standard capacity product
ZEM = Daily standard capacity product
ZEN = Within-day standard capacity product
ZES = Other/Non-standard capacity product
ZET = Balance of month This field indicates the type of the product that is being allocated.
For standard capacity products, the product type should be consistent with the definition set out in Commission Regulation (EU) 2017/459.
For non-standard capacity products, the product type shall be as defined by the OMP or as bilaterally agreed by the counterparties.

Transportation transaction type
<process_Transaction.transactionCode>
ZSF = Primary market procedure Alphanumeric 3 ZSF
ZSZ = Secondary market procedure
ZSP = Capacity conversion
ZSG = Capacity return
ZTL = Buy-back
The field identifies the nature of the relevant transportation transaction to be reported, according to the predefined values for this field.
For secondary allocations, the value ‘ZSZ’ shall be populated in this field. In such cases, Data Field
(33) Procedure must also be populated.
Further examples of the reporting of the above-listed procedures are available in Annex II to the TRUM.
The field is mandatory for primary and secondary allocations.
Data Field (11) Allocation mechanism capacity allocator e.g. TSO, auction operator or the OMP.
<allocationMechanism>
ZSW = Ascending clock auction Alphanumeric 3 ZSW
ZSX = Uniform price auction
ZSY = First come first served
ZTD = Storage allocation
ZTF = Pro-rata
ZTA = Over-nomination
ZTB = Open subscription window

This field indicates the mechanism used by the transmission capacity allocator (e.g. TSO, auction operator or the OMP) to allocate the capacity.
Mechanisms related to over-nominations (‘ZTA’) and open subscription windows (‘ZTB’) shall only refer to the primary market procedure indicated as ‘ZSF’ in Data Field (10) Transportation transaction type.
In the case of secondary market procedures (reported with ‘ZSZ’ in Data Field (10)), this field is not considered applicable.
It is important to note that the alternative allocation mechanism (‘ZTK’) shall be understood as defined in Article 3(3) and Article 30(2) of Commission Regulation (EU) 2017/459.
The field is mandatory for primary allocations.

Offer of additional capacity
<offerOfAdditionalCapacity.additionalCapacityType>
ZTC = Open season Alphanumeric 3 ZTC ZTG = Incremental capacity
This field indicates whether the allocation procedure refers to the offer of additional capacity, such as open season or incremental capacity auctions.
In the case of secondary market procedures (reported with ‘ZSZ’ in Data Field (10)), this field is not considered applicable.

Start date and time
<TimeIntervalType>

End date and time
<TimeIntervalType> ISO 8601 date and time format using Date and time Up to 30 2026-01-29T10:35Z UTC
This field indicates the end date and time of the transportation period (‘transaction runtime’ in the Edig@s schema).
The date and time shall be expressed as ‘YYYY-MM-DDThh:mmZ’.
The field is mandatory for primary and secondary allocations.

Offered capacity
<offeredCapacity_Quantity.quantityAmount>
Up to 32 numerical digits (decimal Numeric Up to 32 200.5 mark included) in the format xxxxx.yyyyy
This field represents the total capacity offered in the specific allocation process (i.e. available capacity offered by the TSO in the auction). This implies that the offered capacity is specific to the allocation process and does not depend on the bidding activity of the market participants.
When reporting the value of the offered capacity in this field, the decimal mark that separates the digits forming the integral part of a number from those forming the fractional part (ISO 6093) shall always be a period (‘.’).
The measurement unit applicable to the offered capacity reported in this field shall be indicated in Data Field (20).
The field is mandatory for allocations occurring via auctions or call for orders procedures.

Capacity category
<process_Transaction.taxonomy.availabilityType>
Z04 = Available total firm capacity Alphanumeric 3 Z06
Z05 = Interruptible (booked)
Z06 = Firm (booked)
ZEQ = Freely allocable capacity
ZER = Capacity with allocation restrictions and usage restrictions

ZET = Dynamically allocable capacity
ZEU = Temperature related and restricted capacity
ZEW = Published technical capacity
ZFA = Available interruptible capacity
ZFB = Available firm capacity
ZFD = Available total interruptible capacity
This field identifies the specific type of capacity allocated based on the relevant allocation procedure.
‘Capacity category’ refers to the result of the allocation procedure (e.g. booked interruptible, booked firm capacity).
The field is mandatory for primary allocations occurring via auctions.

units.b: Data Field (17) Linked auction ID for competing auctions
units.t:
Linked auction ID for competing auctions
<LinkedAuctionId> Up to 35 alphanumerical digits Alphanumeric Up to 35 590825
This field shall identify any auction that is competing with the auction that is being reported and identified in Data Field (3) Process identification. The linked auction ID shall correspond to the code that is uniquely assigned by the OMP hosting the competing auction.
Auctions are considered as competing when competing capacity is being allocated. Competing capacity is defined by Commission Regulation (EU) 2017/459 as ‘capacity for which the available capacity in one of the concerned auctions cannot be allocated without fully or partially reducing the available capacity in the other concerned auction’.
The value reported for the population of this field shall match the relevant auction code, as indicated in any public information issued by the OMP hosting the competing auction.
The field is mandatory in the case of competing auctions.

Action type
<process_Transaction.action_Status.statuscode>
62G = Active Alphanumeric 3 62G
63G = Cancelled
66G = Changed
75G = Correction
This information provided in this field indicates the status of the document.
The sender shall always identify the status of the document according to the following action types. 62G = Active. The report is valid and has never been updated.
63G = Cancelled. The report is not valid anymore as the transaction has been terminated or cancelled before the period runtime starts.
66G = Changed. The report initially submitted had to be modified due to a business decision (e.g. modification of the delivery profile).
75G = Correction. The report initially sent had an error and thus had to be corrected.
The field is mandatory for primary and secondary allocations.

Quantity
<contract_Quantity.quantityAmount>
Up to 32 numerical digits (decimal Numeric Up to 32 20.5 mark included) in the format xxxxx.yyyy
This field identifies the quantity or capacity (in energy per unit of time) for the individual transaction reported, i.e. the contract size, not the total allocated quantity.
The value that shall be reported in this field is the energy per time unit (e.g. the number of kilowatt-hours per hour (kWh/h)), expressed in the measure unit indicated in Data Field (20).
In the case of unsuccessful bids that do not result in allocated capacity, this field shall be populated with the value ‘0’ (zero).
The maximum length of this information is 32 numeric characters (decimal mark included). All leading zeros are to be suppressed. The number of decimal places identifying the fractional part of the quantity depends on local market rules. A decimal point value may be used to express values that are inferior to the defined unit of measurement. The decimal mark that separates the digits forming the integral part of a number from those forming the fractional part (ISO 6093) shall always be a period (‘.’).
The field is mandatory for primary and secondary allocations.

Measure unit
<quantity_measureUnit.code>
KW1 = kilowatt-hour per hour (kWh/h) Alphanumeric 3 KW1
KW2 = kilowatt-hour per day (kWh/d)
HM1 = million cubic meters per hour
HM2 = million cubic meters per day
TQH = thousand cubic meters per hour
TQD = thousand cubic meters per day
MQ6 = normal cubic meters per hour
MQ7 = normal cubic meters per day
KWH = kilowatt-hour (kWh)
GWH = gigawatt-hour (GWh)
This field identifies the unit of measurement used for the quantity information reported in Data Fields (15), (19), (34), (35), (36), (37) and (45). All the quantity information reported for the transaction under the abovementioned data fields shall be expressed in the same unit of measurement.
In the case of allocations concluded on an OMP, the value reported in this field shall correspond to the unit of measurement as advertised by the OMP.
The field is mandatory for primary and secondary allocations.

Currency
<currency.code> EUR = euro Text 3 EUR
EUX = euro cent
CHF = Swiss franc
CHX = centime
CZK = Czech koruna
DKK = Danish krone
DKX = øre
GBP = pound sterling
GBX = penny sterling
HUF = Hungarian forint
ISK = Icelandic króna
NOK = Norwegian krone
PLN = Polish zloty
PLX = grosz
RON = Romanian new leu
ROX = ban
SEK = Swedish krona
USD = US dollar
USX = US cent
This field identifies the currency in which the monetary amounts reported in Data Fields (22), (23), (24), (25), (38), (39) and (44) are expressed, using the smallest denomination in the currency system. All monetary amounts reported for the transaction under the abovementioned data fields shall be expressed in the same currency indicated in Data Field (21).
The price shall be expressed in and consistently reported as price currency per measurement unit per product type, as defined in Data Field (9). This is based on the understanding that the product type identified in Data Field (9) predetermines whether the price is reported per runtime or not.
For example, the transaction report could contain the following information.
• Data Field (20) Measure unit = MWh/h;
• Data Field (21) Currency = EUR;
• Data Field (9) Product type = ZEM (daily standard capacity product);
• Data Field (22) Total price (or whichever price field) = 40;
• Data Field (45) Bid quantity = 10. This would mean that the total price equals 40 €/MWh/h/day, while the bid quantity equals 10 MWh/h. The abovementioned logic for the measure unit and price currency shall be considered applicable to all types of price or quantity information included in the record, except for Data Field (38) Price paid to TSO (underlying price) and Data Field (39) Price the transferee pays to the transferor (both of which are to be expressed in kWh/h).
In the case of allocations concluded on an OMP, the value reported in this field should correspond to the unit of measurement as advertised by the auction platform.
If needed, ACER recommends using the last available European Central Bank foreign exchange reference rate valid for the day of the execution of the transaction for currency conversion.
The field is mandatory for primary and secondary allocations.

Total price
<total_Price.priceAmount>
<contract_Price.priceAmount>
<unit_Price.priceAmount>
Up to 32 numerical digits (decimal Numeric Up to 32 1.8 mark included) in the format xxxxx.yyyyy
This field indicates the total price of the capacity allocated in the primary or secondary allocation. In the case of allocation of bundled capacity, each TSO should report the relevant individual share of the price of the transaction. The individual contributions to the price of those transactions are matched through Data Field (5) Transportation transaction identification.
The price reported in this field shall be expressed in the currency reported in Data Field (21).
The maximum length of the information reported in this field is 32 numeric characters (decimal mark included). All leading zeros are to be suppressed.
It is important to note that the reported total price value should contain both:
• the total price for one unit of the contracted capacity, in the unit of measurement reported in Data Field (22), which shall be equal to the sum of Data Fields (24) and (25); and
• the total price for the total volume of the contracted capacity per network user (i.e. the total contract value). It is ACER’s understanding that, in some cases, it is possible to have a zero (‘0’) reserve price under the tariff methodologies, for example for in-country points or points connected to storage facilities. In such cases, if the auction ends without a premium, the total price reported in this field would also be equal to zero.
The field is mandatory for primary and secondary allocations.

units.b: Data Field (23) Fixed or floating reserve price
units.t:
Fixed or floating reserve price
<reserve_Price.priceCode>
Z01 = Measurement fee Alphanumeric 3 Z07

This field qualifies the type of the reserve price reported in Data Field (24) Reserve price. This implies that the field is always mandatory if Data Field (24) is populated in the case of primary allocations.

Reserve price
<reserve_Price.priceAmount>
Up to 32 numerical digits (decimal mark Numeric Up to 32 1.8 included) in the format xxxxx.yyyyy This field indicates the reserve price for the auction, if applicable. In the case of bundled capacity, each TSO should report its relevant individual share of the price of the transaction.
The price reported in this field shall be expressed in the currency reported in Data Field (21) per unit of measurement, as indicated in Data Field (20).
The field is mandatory for primary allocations and secondary allocations occurring via auctions where a reserve price applies.

Premium price
<premium_Price.priceAmount>
Up to 32 numerical digits (decimal Numeric Up to 32 1.8 mark included) in the format xxxxx.yyyyy
This field indicates the additional amount on top of the reserve price (i.e. the premium price), as agreed between the TSO and the market participant. In the case of bundled capacity, each TSO should report its relevant individual share of the premium of the transaction.
The price reported in this field shall be expressed in the currency reported in Data Field (21) per unit of measurement, as indicated in Data Field (20).
The maximum length of this information is 32 numeric characters (decimal mark included). All leading zeros are to be suppressed.
The field is mandatory for primary and secondary allocations occurring via auctions where a premium applies.

units.b: Data fields related to data for identification of location and market participant
units.t:
Data Field (26) Network point identification <process_Transaction.connectionPoint.identification>
EIC Y Alphanumeric 16 10Y0000123456789
EIC Z
EIC W
This field identifies, by its EIC (type Y, Z or W), the network point that the allocated capacity refers to.
For the validity of the EIC code adopted, reporting parties are invited to refer to the identification code registry provided by ENTSO-E ( ).
In the schema, this field requires the indication of the coding scheme attribute as well. For EIC codes, the coding scheme attribute shall be equal to ‘305’.
The field is mandatory for primary and secondary allocations.

units.t:
Bundling
<process_Transaction.capacityType.code>
ZEO = Bundled capacity Alphanumeric 3 ZEO
ZEP = Unbundled capacity
This field indicates the specification of bundling. The value ‘ZEO’ shall be used for bundled and the value ‘ZEP’ for unbundled capacity.
The field is mandatory for primary and secondary allocations occurring via auctions.
( ) See https://www.entsoe.eu/data/energy-identification-codes-eic/eic-approved-codes/.

Direction
<direction.gasDirectionCode>
Z02 = Input quantity Alphanumeric 3 Z02
Z03 = Output quantity
This field specifies the direction of the transportation capacity in relation to the transmission system operated by the responsible TSO reported in Data Field (29). The TSO sells capacity with a direction in both bundled and unbundled capacity.
The indication of the direction to be reported in this field shall represent the direction of the gas flow in respect of the responsible TSO reported in Data Field (29).
For bundled capacity, the direction reported in this field shall represent the TSO’s side. This implies that, in the case of allocated bundled capacity with direction from TSO A to TSO B (see figure below), this field is expected to be populated with ‘Z03’ when TSO A is identified in Data Field (29) TSO1 identification.
The field is mandatory for primary and secondary allocations.

TSO 1 identification
<process_Transaction.responsibleTso_MarketParticipant.identification>
ACER code Alphanumeric 12 A0643278W.EU 10X0000123456789 EIC 16
This field identifies the TSO that is responsible for the allocated capacity. The responsible TSO shall be identified by a unique identification code, either an ACER code or an EIC code that shall correspond to one of the TSO’s registration codes available in CEREMP.
In the case of primary allocations, this field indicates the TSOs on whose behalf the data reporting is done.
In the schema, this field requires the indication of the coding scheme attribute as well. For EIC codes, the coding scheme attribute shall be equal to ‘305’. For ACER codes, it shall be equal to ‘ACE’.
The field is mandatory for primary and secondary allocations.

TSO 2 identification
<process_Transaction.adjacentTso_MarketParticipant.identification>
ACER code Alphanumeric 12 A0643278W.EU 10X0000123456789 EIC 16
The field identifies the counter TSO by a unique identification code, either an ACER code or an EIC code.
In the schema, this field requires the indication of the coding scheme attribute as well. For EIC codes, the coding scheme attribute shall be equal to ‘305’. For ACER codes, it shall be equal to ‘ACE’.
This field is mandatory for primary allocations only in the case of allocation of bundled capacity (i.e. if Data Field (27) is populated with ‘ZEO’).
For secondary allocations of bundled capacity, this information shall be included only if available to the reporting parties.

Market participant identification
<primary_MarketParticipant.identification>
ACER code Alphanumeric 12 A0643278W.EU 10X1001A1001A450 EIC X 16
This field identifies, by its unique identification code, the market participant the capacity is assigned to.
The identification code of the market participant reported in this field shall correspond to one of the market participants’ registration codes available in CEREMP.
In the schema, this field requires the indication of the coding scheme attribute as well. For EIC codes, the coding scheme attribute shall be equal to ‘305’. For ACER codes, it shall be equal to ‘ACE’.
In the case of primary allocations or allocations occurring via auctions, this field shall also be populated for unsuccessful market participants, i.e. those market participants that inserted a bid but did not succeed in obtaining allocated capacity.
In the case of secondary allocation occurring outside an OMP, this field shall be populated with the market participant on whose behalf the report is sent. The two legs of these transactions shall be matched via the transportation transaction identification provided by both counterparties in Data Field (5).
The field is mandatory for primary and secondary allocations.

units.b: Data Field (32) Balancing group or portfolio code
units.t:
Balancing group or portfolio code
