However, the Agency is aware of the fact that, given the characteristics of some transactions, not all the possible trading scenarios have been covered in this manual. The Agency will continue to work with relevant stakeholders on the reporting of electricity transportation contracts and will provide more detailed information on this topic in subsequent updates of the TRUM, including additional trading scenarios in Annex II.

units.b: Data fields related to common data for total primary and secondary allocation process
units.t:
This section includes the following fields:
Field No. | Field name | Primary allocation | Secondary
allocation
1 | Sender identification | M | M
2 | Organised market place identification | M | M
3 | Process identification | M | M
4 | Type of gas | M* | M*
5 | Transportation transaction identification | M | M
6 | Creation date and time | M | M
7 | Auction open date and time | M* | M*
8 | Auction end date and time | M* | M*
9 | Transportation transaction type | M | M
10 | Start date and time | M | M
11 | End date and time | M | M
12 | Offered capacity | M* | M*
13 | Capacity category | M* | -
M = mandatory
O = optional
- = does not apply
* = conditionally required
DV = default value specified in TRUM

1 | Sender identification | Identification of the party that is the owner of the document and is responsible of its content.
ACER code EIC X | Alphanumeric | 12 16 | A0643278W.EU 10X1001A1001A450
This field indicates the identification of the owner and/or sender of the document. The sender of the document is identified by a unique identification code which shall be either ACER code or EIC X code.
The unique identification code identifies the party that is the “owner” of the information being transmitted in the document and who is responsible for its content. EDIGAS message includes “Standard header information” and requires the indication of the coding scheme attribute. If EIC X code is used for the identification, the coding scheme attribute shall be equal to “305”. For ACER codes, it shall be equal to “ACE”.
The sender may not only be a TSO or a self-reporting market participant, but also a third-party RRM. When the reporting entity is a third-party RRM, the third-party RRM has certain responsibilities for the document content as they have to validate the data they receive from market participants, ensure completeness, accuracy and timely submission of the data according to Article 11(2) of the REMIT Implementing Regulation and, if necessary, correct and resubmit the rejected data in line with Article 11(2) of the REMIT Implementing Regulation. This is why the sender identification has to identify the third-party RRM in cases where a third-party RRM reports.
Both the identification and the coding scheme are mandatory for primary and secondary allocations.
This field corresponds to the field issuer_MarketParticipant.identification in the schema.

units.b: Data Field (2) Organised market place identification
units.t:
2 | Organised market place identification | Identification of organised market place.
ACER code EIC X | Alphanumeric | 12 16 | A0643278W.EU 10X1001A1001A450
This field identifies the organised marketplace or booking platform where the allocation of capacity was executed.
If the allocation was executed at an organised marketplace, the organised marketplace identification field must contain the ACER code as reported in the List of the Organised Market Places published by ACER or Energy Identification Coding (EIC X-type).
If the capacity allocation occurred on a booking platform, different from an organised marketplace, this field is expected to be populated with the identification code (EIC X-type or ACER code) of the relevant operator of the booking platform.
Where the allocation procedure (primary or secondary) does not take place on an organised marketplace or on a booking platforms (e.g. open season process, over-nomination, bilateral allocation), this field should be populated with 21X-XXXXXXXXXXXY.
Both the identification and the coding scheme are mandatory for primary and secondary allocations. If EIC X code is used for the identification, the coding scheme attribute shall be equal to “305”. For ACER codes, it shall be equal to “ACE”.
This field corresponds to the field organisedMarketPlace_MarketParticipant.identification in the schema.

3 | Process identification | The identification of the auction or other process as defined by the capacity allocating entity.
Up to 35 alphanumerical digits. | Alphanumeric | Up to 35 | 590825
This field identifies the auction where the capacity was allocated. The code is uniquely assigned by the auction platform (being an organised marketplace or a booking platform) that hosts the capacity allocation. The process identification should be unique within a particular auction platform, but the same code can also be used by other auction platforms. The value reported for the population of this field shall match the relevant auction code as indicated in public information by the auction platforms.
The field is mandatory also if the capacity was allocated bilaterally (shipper – shipper, TSO – shipper, TSO – network user), outside of an organised marketplace or outside of a booking platform. In such a case, the field shall be populated with an identification code of the allocation agreed bilaterally by the counterparties.
This field corresponds to the field process_Transaction.identification in the schema.
fn: 1 As defined in the Commission Regulation (EU) 2017/459 of 16 March 2017 establishing a network code on capacity allocation mechanisms in gas transmission systems and repealing Regulation (EU) No 984/2013.

units.t:
4 | Type of gas | Identifies the type of gas.
HC1 = High Calorific LC1 = Low Calorific | Alphanumeric | 3 | HC1
The field identifies the type of gas to which the capacity allocation refers to, if with high (H-gas) or low (L-gas) calorific power.
This field is mandatory for allocations occurring via an auction.
This field corresponds to the field process_Transaction.taxonomy.energyProductType in the schema.

5 | Transportation transaction identification | A uniquely assigned identification number for the capacity allocation as assigned by the organised market place or TSO.
Up to 35 digits. | Text | Up to 35 | 111-67A4552
This field provides the identification of the transportation transaction.
For primary allocations, the value reported in this field provides a unique code that clearly identifies primary capacity allocation as assigned by the auction platform or by the TSO.
In case of successful transaction that ends with an allocated capacity to a market participant whose bid is accepted in the auction, the referred unique code that identifies the capacity allocation corresponds to the identifier of the concluded transaction between the TSO and the “successful MP”. Such code is assigned by the auction platform or by the TSO. In case of unmatched orders, that do not end with a transaction and thus with allocated capacity, the referred “unique code” is still assigned by the auction platform or by the TSO with the aim to identify the bidding behaviour of the relevant “unsuccessful MP” during the allocation process. In this framework, the Agency is aware that it is the TSO practice to generate the Transportation transaction identification (for both successful and unsuccessful MPs) as:
Process identification (Data Field (3)), followed by “-“ (dash), followed by the EIC code of the relevant Network User. For secondary allocations, the value reported in this field provides a uniquely assigned identification number for the allocation made between the transferor and transferee as assigned by the Platform Operator or as agreed between the Balancing group(s)/shipper(s) for bilaterally agreed capacity allocations. The value reported in this field by the transferor shall thus be equal to the one reported by the transferee.
This field is mandatory for primary and secondary allocations.
This field corresponds to the field Transportation_Transaction identification in the schema.

units.b: Data Field (6) Creation date and time
units.t:
6 | Creation date and time | Creation date and time of the transaction.
ISO 8601 date and time format using UTC time format. | Date and Time | 30 | 2014-01-29T10:35:56Z
This field indicates the date and time of the execution of the transaction indicating time zone as expressed by ISO 8601 date format / UTC time format (i.e. represents the transaction timestamp). For example, if the allocation occurs via auction, this field shall reflect the time of the announcement of the auction results or any subsequent modifications or cancellations of the trade transaction. However the Agency is aware that sometimes reporting parties might not be in the position to know the exact time of the announcement of the auction results. In such cases, the data field can be populated with the gate closure of the auction. For secondary transaction it means the moment the two counterparties agree upon the conclusion of the deal.
This field is mandatory for primary and secondary allocations.
This field corresponds to the field process_Transaction.transaction_DateTime in the schema.
Clarification on Data Field (6) Creation date and time in the schema
Data Field (6) Creation date and time in TRUM corresponds to the attribute
<process_Transaction.transaction_DateTime.dateTime> in Edig@s schema, and should provide
information on the date and time at which the transaction was executed (i.e. the transaction
timestamp).
TRUM Data Field (6) shall not be confused with element <creationDateTime> in the Edig@s schema,
that reflects the date and time at which the electronic report file was created. The Agency
understands that there might be a delay between the execution time of the transaction and the time
of xml file creation.

units.b: Data Field (7) Auction open date and time
units.t:
7 | Auction open date and time | The date and time when an auction opens for bidding.
ISO 8601 date and time format using UTC time format. | Date and Time | Up to 30 | 2014-01-29T10:35:56Z
This field indicates the date and time when an auction opens for bidding. Auction open date and time expressed by ISO 8601 date format / UTC time format.
This field is mandatory if the primary or secondary allocations occurs via auctions but shall be left blank if the process of allocation does not involve an auction or call for orders.
This field corresponds to the field process_Transaction.auctionOpen_DateTime in the schema.

units.b: Data Field (8) Auction end date and time
units.t:
8 | Auction end date and time | The date and time when an auction closes.
ISO 8601 date and time format using UTC time format. | Date and Time | Up to 30 | 2014-01-29T10:35:56Z
This field indicates the date and time when an auction closes for bidding, i.e. the last point in time when a participant to that market can submit orders and when trading can occur. Auction End Date and Time as expressed by ISO 8601 date format / UTC time format.
For primary or secondary allocations via auction markets, this field is mandatory and shall reflect the gate closure.
If the process of allocation does not involve an auction (e.g. secondary allocations outside an organised marketplace), or in case of call for orders, this field shall be left blank.
This field corresponds to the field process_Transaction.auctionEnd_DateTime in the schema.

9 | Transportation transaction type | The type identifies the nature of transportation transaction to be reported in accordance with current applicable industry standards as specified by Gas Network code on Interoperability and Data Exchange.
ZSW = Ascending clock auction ZSX = Uniform price auction ZSY = First come first served ZSZ = Secondary market procedure ZTA = Over-nomination ZTB = Open Subscription Window ZTC = Open season ZTD = Storage allocation ZTE = Non-ascending clock pay-as-bid auction ZTF = Pro-rata ZSP = Capacity conversion | Alphanumeric | 3 | Z SX
ZSG = Capacity return
The field identifies the nature of specific transportation transaction to be reported choosing among the values reported above.
For secondary allocations, transactions shall be reported populating this field with ZSZ.
This field is mandatory for primary and secondary allocations.
This field corresponds to the field process_Transaction.type in the schema.
Examples of the transaction reporting of the above procedures are available in the Annex II of TRUM.

units.b: Data Field (10) Start date and time
units.t:
10 | Start date and time | Date and time of the start of the transportation transaction runtime.
ISO 8601 date and time format using UTC time format. | Date and Time | Up to 30 | 2018-01-29T04:00Z
This field indicates the start date and time of the transportation period (“transaction runtime” in the Edig@s schema). Date and time shall be expressed as: YYYY-MM-DDThh:mmZ.
This field is mandatory for primary and secondary allocations.
The information on the Start date and time of the transaction period corresponds to the first value to be reported in the field Transportation_Period timeInterval in the schema.

units.b: Data Field (11) End date and time
units.t:
11 | End date and time | Date and time of the end of the transportation transaction runtime.
ISO 8601 date and time format using UTC time format. | Date and Time | Up to 30 | 2014-01-29T10:35Z
This field indicates the end date and time of the transportation period (“transaction runtime” in the Edig@s schema). Date and time shall be expressed as: YYYY-MM-DDThh:mmZ.
This field is mandatory for primary and secondary allocations.
The information on the End date and time of the transaction period corresponds to the second value to be reported in the field Transportation_Period timeInterval in the schema.

12 | Offered capacity | The quantity of capacity available in the auction expressed in the measure unit. Only relevant for bidding behaviour monitoring.
Up to 17 numerical digits (decimal mark included) in the format xxxxx.yyyyy. | Number | Up to 17 | 200.5
The field represents the total quantity of capacity offered in the specific allocation process (i.e. offered capacity by the TSO in the auction). Hence such value is allocation-process-specific and does not depend on the bidding activity of the market participants.
The value that shall be reported in this field is the capacity available in the auction or call for orders expressed in the Measure unit indicated in Data Field (16).
The decimal mark that separates the digits forming the integral part of a number from those forming the fractional part (ISO 6093) shall always be a period (“.”).
This field is mandatory for allocations occurring via auctions or call for orders procedures.
This field corresponds to the field offeredCapacity_Quantity.amount in the schema.

13 | Capacity category | Applicable capacity category.
Z04 = Available total firm capacity Z05 = Interruptible (booked) Z06 = Firm (booked) ZEQ = Freely allocable capacity ZER = Capacity with allocation restrictions and usage restrictions ZES = Restricted-allocable capacity ZET = Dynamically allocable capacity ZEU = Temperature related and restricted capacity ZEW = Published technical capacity ZFA = Available interruptible capacity ZFB = Available firm capacity ZFD = Available total interruptible c apacity | Alphanumeric | 3 | Z06
The field identifies the specific type of capacity allocated based on the particular allocation procedure. Capacity category refers to the result of the allocation procedure (booked interruptible, booked firm capacity).
This field is mandatory for primary allocations occurring via auctions.
This field corresponds to the field process_Transaction.taxonomy.AvailabilityType in the schema.

This section includes the following fields:
Field No. | Field name | Primary allocation | Secondary allocation
14 | Action type | M | M
M = mandatory
O = optional
- = does not apply
* = conditionally required
DV = default value specified in TRUM

14 | Action type | Status code of the report to be reported in accordance with current applicable industry standards as specified in Gas Network code on Interoperability and Data Exchange.
62G = Active. 63G = Cancelled. 66G = Changed. 75G = Correction. | Alphanumeric | 3 | 62G
This information provides the status of the document.
The sender indicates if the report submitted is valid and never modified, updated, due to erroneous previous submission, updated due to business decision or not valid anymore: 62G = Active. This data means that the report is valid and has never been updated. 63G = Cancelled. This data means that the report is not valid anymore as the contract has been terminated or cancelled before the period runtime starts. 66G = Changed. This data means that the report initially submitted had to be modified due to a business decision (e.g. modification of the delivery profile). 75G = Correction. This data means that the report initially sent had an error and thus had to be corrected.
This field is mandatory for primary and secondary allocations.
This field corresponds to the field process_Transaction.action_Status.code in the schema.

units.b: Data fields for quantity and price reporting
units.t:
This section includes the following fields:
Field No. | Field name | Primary allocation | Secondary allocation
15 | Quantity | M | M
16 | Measure unit | M | M
17 | Currency | M | M
18 | Total price | M | M
19 | Fixed or floating reserve price | M* | -
20 | Reserve price | M* | M*
21 | Premium price | M* | M*
M = mandatory
O = optional
- = does not apply
* = conditionally required
DV = default value specified in TRUM

15 | Quantity | Total number of units allocated with the transportation transaction as expressed in the measure unit.
Up to 17 numerical digits (decimal mark included) in the format x xxxx.yyyyy. | Number | Up to 17 | 20.5
This field identifies the quantity or capacity (energy per unit of time) for the contract, i.e. the contract size. The value that shall be reported in this field is the energy per time unit, e.g. the number of kW (i.e. kWh/h), expressed in the measure unit indicated in Data Field (16).
In case of unmatched orders (“unsuccessful MP”), that does not end with a transaction and thus with allocated capacity, this field should be populated with “0” (zero).
The maximum length of this information is 17 numeric characters (decimal mark included). All leading zeros are to be suppressed. The number of decimal places identifying the fractional part of the quantity depends on local market rules. A decimal point value may be used to express values that are inferior to the defined unit of measurement. The decimal mark that separates the digits forming the integral part of a number from those forming the fractional part (ISO 6093) shall always be a period (“.”).
This field is mandatory for primary and secondary allocations.
This field corresponds to the field contract_Quantity.amount in the schema.

16 | Measure unit | The unit of measurement used.
KW1 = Kilowatt-hour per hour (kWh/h) KW2 = Kilowatt-hour per day (kWh/d) HM1 = Million cubic meters per hour HM2 = Million cubic meters per day TQH = Thousand cubic meters per hour TQD = Thousand cubic meters per day MQ6 = Normal cubic meters per hour MQ7 = Normal cubic meters per day KWH = Kilowatt hour (kWh) GWH= Gigawatt hour (GWh) | Alphanumeric | 3 | KW1
This field identifies the unit of measurement used for the reported quantity in Data Field (12), Data Field
(15) and Data Field (41).
In case of allocations concluded on an organised marketplace or on a booking platform, the value reported in this field should correspond to the unit as advertised by the auction platform.
This field is mandatory for primary and secondary allocation.
This field corresponds to the field quantity_MeasureUnit.code in the schema.

17 | Currency | The currency in which the monetary amount is expressed.
EUR = Euro BGN = Bulgarian lev CHF = Swiss franc CZK = Czech koruna DKK = Danish krone GBP = Pound sterling HUF = Hungarian forint ISK = Icelandic króna NOK = Norwegian krone PLN = Polish złoty RON = Romanian new leu SEK = Swedish krona/kronor USD = U.S. dollar | Text | 3 | E UR
This field identifies the currency in which the monetary amount is expressed (currency of the price using the smallest denomination in the currency system). If needed, the Agency recommends using the last available European Central Bank foreign exchange reference rate for the currency conversion valid for the day of the execution of the transaction.
This field is mandatory for primary and secondary allocations.
This field corresponds to the field currency.code in the schema.

18 | Total price | Reserve price at time of the auction plus auction premium or regulated tariff in case of other allocation mechanism than auction.
Up to 17 numerical digits (decimal mark included) in the format x xxxx.yyyyy. | Number | Up to 17 | 1 .8
This field indicates the total price of the unit of allocated capacity, being primary or secondary. In case of allocation of bundled capacity, each TSO should report the relevant individual share of the price of the transaction. The individual contributions to the price of those transactions are matched through Data Field (5), i.e. transportation transaction identification.
The price reported in this field shall be expressed in the currency reported in Data Field (17). It is worth noticing that the reported Total price value should be valid for one unit of the contracted capacity but not for the price of the total volume of the contracted capacity per network user.
In case of both bundled and unbundled capacity, the value reported in this field should correspond to the sum of Data Field (20) and Data Field (21). The maximum length of this information is 17 numeric characters (decimal mark included). All leading zeros are to be suppressed.
This field is mandatory for primary and secondary allocations.
This field corresponds to the field total_Price.amount in the schema.
Population of Data Field (18) in case of zero premium and reserve price
The Agency is aware that on some occasions it is possible to have a zero (0) reserve price according
to the tariff methodologies, e.g. for in-country points or points connected to storage facilities. In such
cases, if the auction ends without premium, the total price reported in Data Field (18) would be also
equal to zero.

units.b: Data Field (19) Fixed or floating reserve price
units.t:
19 | Fixed or floating reserve price | Identification of the type of the reserve price.
Z07 = Fixed Price Z08 = Floating Price | Alphanumeric | 3 | Z07
This field is mandatory if Data Field (20) Reserve price is populated in primary allocations. The field qualifies the type of the reserve price reported in Data Field (20).
This field corresponds to the field reserve_Price.type in the schema.

20 | Reserve price | The identification of the reserve price for the auction.
Up to 17 numerical digits (decimal mark included) in the format x xxxx.yyyyy. | Number | Up to 17 | 1 .8
This field identifies the reserve price for the auction, if applicable. In case of bundled capacity, each TSO should report the relevant individual share of the price of the transaction.
The price reported in this field shall be expressed in the currency reported in Data Field (17) per unit of measurement as indicated in Data Field (16). This field is mandatory for allocations occurring via auctions (primary allocations and secondary if occurred via auctions) where a reserve price applies.
This field corresponds to the field reserve_Price.amount in the schema.

21 | Premium price | The identification of the premium price for the auction.
Up to 17 numerical digits (decimal mark included) in the format x xxxx.yyyyy. | Number | Up to 17 | 1 .8
This field identifies the additional amount on top of the reserve price as agreed between TSO and the market participant. In case of bundled capacity, each TSO should report the relevant individual share of the premium of the transaction.
The price reported in this field shall be expressed in the currency reported in Data Field (17) per unit of measurement as indicated in Data Field (16).
The maximum length of this information is 17 numeric characters (decimal mark included). All leading zeros are to be suppressed.
This field is mandatory for allocations occurring via auctions (primary allocations and secondary if occurred via auctions) where a premium applies.
This field corresponds to the field premium_Price.amount in the schema.

units.b: Data fields for identification of location and market participant
units.t:
This section includes the following fields:
Field No. | Field name | Primary allocation | Secondary allocation
22 | Network point identification | M | M
23 | Bundling | M* | M*
24 | Direction | M | M
25 | TSO 1 identification | M | M
26 | TSO 2 Identification | M* | M*
27 | Market participant identification | M | M
28 | Balancing group or portfolio code | M* | M*
M = mandatory
O = optional
- = does not apply
* = conditionally required
DV = default value specified in TRUM

22 | Network point identification | Within a network system according to the EIC code.
EIC Y, Z or W | Alphanumeric | 16 | 10Y0000123456789
This field identifies the network point to which the allocated capacity refers to. The identification of the network point occurs via the indication of the EIC code (type Y, Z or W). For the validity of the EIC code adopted, reporting parties are invited to refer to the identification code registry provided by ENTSO-E . In the schema, this field requires the indication of the coding scheme attribute as well. For EIC codes, the coding scheme attribute shall be equal to “305”.
The field is mandatory for primary and secondary allocations.
This field corresponds to the field process_Transaction.connectionPoint.identification – CODINGSCHEME in the schema.

23 | Bundling | Specification of bundling.
ZEO = Bundled capacity ZEP = Unbundled capacity | Alphanumeric | 3 | ZEO
This field is represented in the EDIGAS schema as “CapacityType.CODE” and the code for “bundled” is “ZEO” and that for unbundled is “ZEP”.
This field is mandatory for allocations occurring via auctions (primary allocations and secondary if occurred via auctions).
This field corresponds to the field process_Transaction.capacityType.code in the schema.

24 | Direction | Specification of direction.
Z02 = Input Quantity Z03 = Output Quantity | Alphanumeric | 3 | Z 02
This field specifies the direction of the transportation capacity in relation to the transmission system operated by the responsible TSO reported in Data Field (25). The TSO sells capacity with a direction in both bundled and unbundled capacity. This field is mandatory for primary and secondary allocations.
This field corresponds to the field direction.code in the schema.
Clarifications on the Data Field (24) Direction
The indication of the direction to be reported in Data Field (24) should represent the direction of the gas flow in respect to the responsible TSO reported in Data Field (25).
Figure 4: Identification of the direction for gas transportation transactions
For bundled capacity, the direction field represents the TSO's side. Hence in case of allocated bundled capacity with direction from TSO A to TSO B (see Figure 4), this field is expected to be populated with “Z03” when Data Field (25) TSO1 identification reports TSO A.
fn: 1 EIC CODES (entsoe.eu)

units.t:
25 | TSO 1 identification | The identification of the TSO for which the data reporting is made.
ACER code EIC | Alphanumeric | 12 16 | A0643278W.EU 10X0000123456789
This field identifies the responsible TSO for the allocated capacity. In case of primary allocations, this field indicates the TSOs on whose behalf the data reporting is made.
The responsible TSO shall be identified by a unique identification code, either ACER code or EIC code.
In the schema, this field requires the indication of the coding scheme attribute as well. For EIC codes, the coding scheme attribute shall be equal to “305”. For ACER codes, it shall be equal to “ACE”.
The identifier reported in this field shall correspond to the relevant one listed in CEREMP.
The field is mandatory for primary and secondary allocations.
This field corresponds to the field process_Transaction.responsibleTso_MarketParticipant.identification
– CODINGSCHEME in the schema.

26 | TSO 2 identification | The identification of the counter TSO.
ACER code EIC | Alphanumeric | 12 16 | A0643278W.EU 10X0000123456789
This field is mandatory for primary allocations if Data Field (23) is filled in with ZEO, i.e. only in case of allocation of bundled capacity. For secondary allocations of bundled capacity, this information shall be included if available to the reporting parties.
TSO 2 shall be identified by a unique identification code, either ACER code or EIC code.
In the schema, this field requires the indication of the coding scheme attribute as well. For EIC codes, the coding scheme attribute shall be equal to “305”. For ACER codes, it shall be equal to “ACE”.
This field corresponds to the field process_Transaction.adjacentTso_MarketParticipant.identification – codingscheme in the schema.

27 | Market participant identification | The market participant to which the capacity is assigned.
ACER code E IC X-type | Alphanumeric | 12 16 | A0643278W.EU 1 0X1001A1001A450
This field identifies the market participant to which the capacity is assigned.
The identification code (i.e. ACER code or EIC X code) reported in this field shall correspond to the code assigned to or provided by the relevant Market Participant in CEREMP as part of its registration under Article 9 of Regulation (EU) No 1227/2011. In case of primary allocations or allocations occurring via auctions, this field shall be populated also in case of unsuccessful market participants, i.e. those market participants that inserted a bid but did not succeed in getting an allocated capacity.
In case of secondary allocation occurring outside an organised marketplace, this field shall be populated with the market participant on whose behalf the report is sent. The two legs of those transactions are matched through Data Field (5), i.e. transportation transaction identification.
This field is mandatory for primary and secondary allocations.
In the schema, this field requires the indication of the coding scheme attribute as well. For EIC codes, the coding scheme attribute shall be equal to “305”. For ACER codes, it shall be equal to “ACE”.
This field corresponds to the field primary_MarketParticipant.identification – CODINGSCHEME in the schema.

units.b: Data Field (28) Balancing group or portfolio code
units.t:
28 | Balancing group or portfolio code | The balancing group (or balancing groups in case of bundled products) to which the shipper belongs
or the portfolio code used by the shipper if a balancing group is not applicable.
TSO managed code (ZSO) E IC | Alphanumeric | Up to 35 16 | 10X0000123456789
This field is mandatory for both primary and secondary allocations only where balancing group portfolio or accounts apply.
Internal account (i.e. identification) of the shipper or the balancing group account (i.e. identification) assigned by the responsible TSO (identified in Data Field (25) TSO 1 Identification) needs to be reported in this field.
In the schema, this field requires the indication of the coding scheme attribute as well. For a TSO managed code (IS-U code), the coding scheme attribute shall be equal to “ZSO”. For EIC codes, the coding scheme attribute shall be equal to “305”.
This field corresponds to the field primary_MarketParticipant.account.internalAccount in the schema.

units.b: Data fields applicable only for secondary allocations
units.t:
This section includes the following fields:
Field No. | Field name | Primary allocation | Secondary allocation
29 | Procedure applicable | - | M
30 | Maximum bid amount | - | M*
31 | Minimum bid amount | - | M*
32 | Maximum quantity | - | M*
33 | Minimum quantity | M* | M*
34 | Price paid to TSO (underlying price) | - | M*
35 | Price the transferee pays to the transferor | - | M
36 | Transferor identification | - | M
37 | Transferee identification | - | M
M = mandatory
O = optional
- = does not apply
* = conditionally required
DV = default value specified in TRUM

29 | Procedure applicable | Specification of procedure applicable.
A01 = CFO, Call for orders for Alphanumeric 3 A01 assignment A02 = FCFS, First come first served for assignment A03 = OTC, Over the counter for assignment A04 = CFO_SUB, Call for orders for subletting / transfer of use A05 = FCFS_SUB, First come first served for subletting / transfer of use A06 = OTC_SUB, Over the counter for subletting / transfer of use.
This field identifies the specific secondary allocation procedure and is thus mandatory only in the case of secondary market allocations.
This field corresponds to the field process_Transaction.secondaryMarket_Procedure.code in the schema.

30 | Maximum bid amount | The maximum the transferee would be willing to offer, expressed in the currency per measure unit.
Up to 17 numerical digits (decimal mark included) in the format xxxxx.yyyyy. | Number | Up to 17 | 1.8
This field indicates the maximum price the transferee is willing to pay when participating to a call for orders procedure. This field is thus mandatory only for “Call for orders” procedure, i.e. when Data Field
(29) is populated with A01.
The value reported in this field shall be expressed in the currency reported in Data Field (17) per capacity unit as expressed in data Field (16).
The maximum length of this information is 17 numeric characters (decimal mark included). All leading zeros are to be suppressed.
This field corresponds to the field maximumBid_Price.amount in the schema.

31 | Minimum bid amount | The minimum the transferor would be willing to offer, expressed in the currency per measure unit.
Up to 17 numerical digits (decimal mark included) in the format x xxxx.yyyyy. | Number | Up to 17 | 1 .8
This field indicates the minimum price the transferor is willing to accept within a call for orders procedure. This field is thus mandatory only for “Call for orders” procedure, i.e. when Data Field (29) is populated with A01.
The value reported in this field shall be expressed in the currency reported in Data Field (17) per capacity unit as expressed in data Field (16).

units.b: Legal framework and purpose of reporting
units.t: Regulation (EU) No 1227/2011 on wholesale energy market integrity and transparency (REMIT) ( ) has established a sector-specific framework for the monitoring of wholesale energy markets, with the objective of detecting and deterring insider trading and market manipulation. Due to the significant evolution of EU wholesale energy markets since REMIT was first introduced in 2011, the regulation has been revised, namely via amending Regulation (EU) 2024/1106 ( ), which entered into force on 7 May 2024. As a result of the revision, the scope of REMIT was expanded to cover additional products and markets. One of the key novelties was the introduction of the obligation on market participants to report information about their exposures, as part of the reporting obligations under Article 8 of REMIT. Recast Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/256 (REMIT Implementing Regulation) ( ) further clarified in Article 6 the context and details of exposure reporting under REMIT: market participants shall report positions resulting from trading wholesale energy products and, upon request of the European Union Agency for the Cooperation of Energy Regulators (ACER) and for the purpose of establishing exposures, information about their forecasted volumes of electricity or natural gas, including liquefied natural gas (LNG), and production and information about their forecasted volumes of consumption of electricity or natural gas based on contracts concluded with their customers. The reported information on market participants’ exposures is intended to complement the REMIT dataset, i.e. to be analysed in combination with the other data received by ACER under REMIT, in order to facilitate detection of potential instances of market abuse or dismiss suspicions of such cases. This guidance aims to provide market participants with clarifications on their reporting obligations in relation to exposure reporting, and detailed descriptions and instructions for the related reporting requirements, in order to enable them to comply with the relevant regulatory requirements. EU legislation is legally binding and establishes rights, obligations and requirements that must be complied with by legal or natural persons to which it applies. In the context of transaction reporting under REMIT, market participants must submit all reportable information in accordance with the transaction reporting user manual (TRUM), including its annexes, as foreseen in Article 7(4) of Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/256.

ACER invites stakeholders wishing to address questions relating to exposure reporting under REMIT to always refer to ACER’s REMIT Query Form available on the REMIT Documents section of the ACER website.
( ) Regulation (EU) No 1227/2011 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 25 October 2011 on wholesale energy market integrity and transparency (OJ L 326, 8.12.2011, pp. 1–16, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg/2011/1227/oj). ( ) Regulation (EU) 2024/1106 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 11 April 2024 amending Regulations (EU) No 1227/2011 and (EU) 2019/942 as regards improving the Union’s protection against market manipulation on the wholesale energy market (OJ L, 2024/1106, 17.4.2024, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1106/oj). ( ) Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/256 of 30 January 2026 on data reporting implementing Article 7c(2), Article 8(1a), Article 8(2) and Article 8(6) of Regulation (EU) No 1227/2011 of the European Parliament and of the Council on wholesale energy market integrity and transparency and repealing Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) No 1348/2014 (OJ L, 2026/256, 9.4.2026, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg_impl/2026/256/oj).

For the definition of ‘market participant’, Article 2(7) of REMIT also applies in the context of exposure reporting. In accordance with Article 8(1), market participants shall report records of their transactions on wholesale energy markets, including information on their exposures. Consequently, only market participants that enter into reportable transactions and are obliged to report records of their transactions under the regulation can be subject to the obligation to report information about their exposures. Furthermore, market participants only engaging in transactions referred to in Article 5(1)(b), 5(1)(c) or 5(1)(d) of the REMIT Implementing Regulation, hence, not required to register with their national regulatory authority (NRA) pursuant to Article 9(1) of REMIT, are considered to fall outside the perimeter of market participants subject to the exposure reporting obligation. The scope of market participants subject to the exposure reporting obligation is further narrowed by Article 6 of the REMIT Implementing Regulation. More specifically, Article 6(5) foresees that market participants with positions, as defined in Article 6(2), below 600 gigawatt-hours (GWh) on a yearly basis, assessed separately for electricity and natural gas, shall not be required to submit exposure reports (i.e. neither positions nor forecasts) during the referred calendar year for which the assessment was carried out. The provision set in Article 6(5) implies that market participants with positions ( ) equal to or above 600 GWh on a yearly basis, calculated separately for electricity and natural gas, are required to submit information on their positions during the referred calendar year for which the assessment was carried out. The same entities are also eligible for the reporting, at the request of ACER, of the forecasted production and consumption information. It is important to note that the calculation for the assessment against the yearly threshold shall consider the very same perimeter of transactions, including the scope of commodities, relating to wholesale energy products that is specified for the quarterly position reporting obligation in Section 3.1. The yearly assessment against the threshold set in Article 6(5) is to be carried out by considering the relevant values at the end of each calendar year (Y ) relating to the market participant’s entire positions n within the predefined perimeters for delivery / settlement in the upcoming calendar year (1 January– 31 December in Y ). This implies that any trading done on 31 December (Y ) shall be included in n + 1 n the assessment as well. In ACER’s understanding, this may imply that in order to ensure that the calculation of the positions includes all transactions concluded until the end of 31 December Y , market participants may need to n carry out the assessment for Y in early Y . Nevertheless, market participants equal to or above n + 1 n + 1 the threshold must ensure that they are ready to comply with their exposure reporting obligation by the legal deadline the reporting of the first reference quarter of the relevant year is due, based on the result of their assessment. Article 17(2) of the REMIT Implementing Regulation specifies that the exposure reporting obligation shall apply from 1 January 2027. This means that as of 1 January 2027, REMIT market participants shall perform their assessment on the threshold for the 2027 calendar year (and, if it is equal to or above the threshold, begin the reporting in October 2027 for Q3 2027). Methodology for the threshold assessment
In order for market participants to assess whether they have to report exposure in a given calendar year Y , as of the end of Y (being the cut-off date) they must follow the steps shown below. n + 1 n Review their positions, including intragroup transactions, referring to wholesale energy products with delivery in Y based on the transactions concluded until the end of Y . n + 1 n

(1) Aggregate the positions per commodity.
(2) Aggregate the positions per delivery month in Y (per commodity). n + 1
(3) Sum up the absolute monthly values.
(4) If a market participant has positions in more than one country, this assessment must be carried out for each country and then the absolute values must be summed up for all relevant countries.

(5) Compare the final value with the threshold of 600 GWh/year, separately for electricity and natural gas. If the sum of the absolute monthly values is below the threshold, the market participant will not have to report its positions referred to the specific commodity throughout Y . n + 1 Given the monthly granularity and country-level split of the position reporting obligation set out in Articles 6(2) and 6(3) of the REMIT Implementing Regulation, a monthly granularity shall be taken into consideration also for the threshold assessment, aggregating at the country level. Market participants falling in scope of exposure reporting (i.e. reaching the threshold as a result of the market participant’s individual assessment) shall submit a position report for the relevant commodity
( ) When dealing with the exposure reporting obligation, in line with other reporting obligations set in the REMIT Implementing Regulation, the concept of ‘position’ is intended to be the result from the market participant’s trading activity on wholesale energy products where the delivery is in the EU. (and, upon request, the forecasted production and consumption information) in every quarter (i.e. reference period) in the relevant calendar year Y . n + 1 The yearly assessment shall be considered as an annual exercise to be performed once a year. This implies that market participants do not need to reassess their yearly positions against the threshold during the given calendar year (e.g. by taking into account subsequent trading activity for the given year, which potentially could alter the threshold assessment). This applies irrespective of whether the reassessment would result in a change to the market participant’s ‘status’ (i.e. where a reassessment of a market participant originally below the threshold would result in them reaching above the threshold). While market participants are not expected to submit to ACER the results of their yearly assessments, they are expected to be able to provide their assessment to ACER or NRAs upon request for the upcoming five years after the assessment takes place. This requirement does not apply to market participants that, following their assessment for the relevant calendar year, fall within the scope of the exposure reporting obligation and are therefore required to report their exposure information to ACER on a quarterly basis during that calendar year. Market participants falling under the scope of the exposure reporting obligation must bear in mind that they are responsible for complying with the data quality reporting requirements, including completeness, accuracy and timeliness of the reported exposure information. In case of a need for further clarification, ACER may request market participants to provide information and clarifications in relation to the reported exposure information as empowered by Article 6(7) of the REMIT Implementing Regulation. Obligation for TSOs, DSOs, SSOs and LSOs
Article 6(6) specifies that transmission system operators (TSOs), distribution system operators (DSOs), storage system operators (SSOs) and LNG system operators (LSOs) that purchase natural gas or electricity solely for the technological or operational needs of the system they operate are only required to report their exposure information (i.e. positions and forecasts information) upon the request of ACER. This implies that TSOs, DSOs, SSOs and LSOs are exempted from the exposure reporting unless explicitly requested to report by ACER and, as such, are not considered to be subject to the threshold assessment ( ).
fn: 600 GWh/year, the market participant will not have to report, provided this is the only country with positions.

units.t:
As set out in Article 6(1) of the REMIT Implementing Regulation, exposure reports shall be submitted to ACER once per quarter (‘reference period’), and no later than the last day of the month following the
( ) For further information, see the ACER open letter on the implications of the REMIT Implementing Regulation on data reporting. last day of the reference period. The reference period shall be understood, and hereafter referred to, as the reference quarter. In addition, whenever referring to ‘exposure reporting’, it is intended to refer primarily to the periodic reporting of positions and, upon request, complemented with the forecasted production and consumption information. It is crucial for market participants to understand the different timelines relevant for the exposure reporting. Timeline for reporting
The requirement set out in Article 6(1) of the REMIT Implementing Regulation means that the exposure reporting constitutes a quarterly reporting where the deadline for reporting the exposure information relating to the given reference quarter is no later than the last day of the month following the reference quarter. Timeline for the calculation
By the predefined deadline for reporting at the latest, the exposure elements relevant for the given reference quarter shall be calculated by taking into account the relevant contracts, i.e. contracts with delivery/settlement within the next 18 months. The cut-off date for the relevant contracts to be included in the calculation in the given reference quarter is the last day of the reference quarter. This means that the positions as of the last day of the reference quarter shall be considered the basis for the calculation, irrespective of whether the related trading activity occurred before the reference quarter. The relevant trading activities occurring on the last day of the reference quarter shall always be considered in the calculation. The indications above imply that multi-year (long-term) supply contracts, still in delivery in any of the next 18 months belonging to the reference quarter, must be included in the position calculation, irrespective of the fact that the signing of the contract occurred before the reference quarter. Delivery window
The delivery window to be considered relevant for the exposure reporting is 18 months starting from the first month after the reference quarter. This implies that contracts with delivery in the next 18 months shall be considered in the calculation and the reporting. Relevant dates for reporting
The first reporting shall take place in October 2027. This implies that by 31 October 2027 at the latest, market participants subject to the exposure reporting obligation in 2027 ( ) shall submit the first exposure report to ACER via their designated RRM. For this specific reporting, the reference quarter is the third quarter of 2027 (Q3 2027), and the 18-month delivery timeline that must be considered for calculating the exposure is the period between 1 October 2027 and 31 March 2029. For the purpose of exposure reporting under REMIT, ‘positions’ shall be understood as the accumulated (net) volume of energy resulting from trading wholesale energy products by the market participant. In the context of position reporting, only contracts for the supply of energy shall be considered to be in the scope, therefore the definition of a wholesale energy product set out in Article 2(4)(a) and 2(4)(b) of REMIT shall be taken into consideration. More specifically, ‘wholesale energy products’ means the following contracts and derivatives, irrespective of where and how they are traded:
(a) contracts for the supply of electricity or natural gas, including LNG, where delivery is in the Union, or contracts for the supply of electricity which may result in delivery in the Union as a result of single day-ahead and intraday coupling; and
(b) derivatives relating to electricity or natural gas produced, traded or delivered in the Union, or derivatives relating to electricity which may result in delivery in the Union as a result of single day-ahead and intraday coupling.
Market participants must keep in mind that the REMIT transaction reporting and the exposure reporting framework serve different purposes, so their scope and reporting structure may differ. Commodities in scope
The above definition specifies that contracts relating to electricity and natural gas shall be considered. In case of natural gas, the following considerations shall be taken into account for the purpose of position calculation:
• transactions relating to the supply of LNG shall be considered as natural gas commodity.
• with regard to biogas (including biomethane), if it can technically and safely be injected into, and transported through, the natural gas system, it will: (i) meet all criteria to be treated as natural gas, and (ii) REMIT will apply for the biogas supply/transportation contracts ( ), hence it will be considered in the calculation as natural gas. In addition, wholesale energy products relating to the supply of hydrogen are not envisaged to be included in the position calculation.
( ) See Chapter 2 in the Guideline on REMIT transaction reporting EU perimeter in scope
The above definition of a ‘wholesale energy product’ specifies that for the purposes of position reporting, only transactions resulting from the market participant’s trading activity where there is EU delivery shall be taken into account. It is also important to note that in the context of position reporting, the above definition of a wholesale energy product implies that if the wholesale energy product is traded on a venue located outside the EU but specifies EU delivery, the trading positions in such wholesale energy product will be considered in the scope of the position reporting obligation. In addition, in the context of LNG trades concluded on an ‘Free on board’ (FOB) basis (where the buyer acquires the LNG and is responsible for shipping, so that the delivery country may not be specified in the original contract), traded volumes relating to EU deliveries shall be considered for the position calculation. This implies that if an FOB contract specifies potential EU delivery (even if without a fixed EU LNG terminal at the time of the agreement), it shall be included in the calculation. Market timeframe and delivery horizon

While the definition of a wholesale energy product gives the general indication on the scope of position reporting, the market timeframe where the wholesale energy product is traded may limit the scope further. This means that positions relating to transactions for supply concluded on spot markets (e.g. day-ahead and intraday timeframes) are out of scope of the position calculation. Such a requirement relies on the forward-looking nature of the exposure reporting obligation, therefore spot market data from the day-ahead and intraday timeframes shall not be taken into considered for the sake of position reporting. In addition, for electricity and natural gas (not including LNG) contracts with delivery duration of one week or less (e.g. balance of week contracts or balance of month with delivery less than a week) should also not be included in positions calculation. It is important to note that as per established industry terminology, the term ‘spot’ shall be interpreted differently in case of LNG trades. In ACER’s understanding, in LNG trading the term ‘spot’ shall not be understood as a reference to the close proximity of the delivery window of the cargo. The delivery window is specified in the spot-type contract, but it does not necessarily refer to a near term (or spot) delivery, meaning that the agreed delivery is to be executed at a pre-specified, usually future point in time (i.e. several months after the agreement). Therefore, all LNG spot trades shall still be taken into consideration. Financially settled derivatives
With regard to transactions relating to derivatives falling under the scope of REMIT (see the above-mentioned definition of ‘wholesale energy product’) but reported under the financial regulation shall still be included in the position calculation. Transactions in scope
Provided the perimeters explained above for the position reporting are respected, in general market participants will consider for their position calculations transactions that relate to supply contracts falling under the scope of the continuous reporting obligation of Article 3(a) of the REMIT Implementing Regulation. However, it is important to note that while intragroup transactions relating to contracts for supply that were concluded bilaterally are to be reported at the request of ACER pursuant to Article 5(1)(a) of the REMIT Implementing Regulation, these do fall under the exposure reporting perimeter as per Article 6(2) of the REMIT Implementing Regulation requiring differentiation between intragroup versus non-intragroup positions. The differentiation between intragroup vs non-intragroup positions when performing the quarterly reporting shall be carried out in line with the group definition established by the reporting market participant for the purpose of exposure reporting (see Section 3.2). It is also important to recall that market participants concluding only transactions that fall under Article 5(1)(a) of the REMIT Implementing Regulation are bound by the registration obligation with their respective NRA under Article 9(1) of REMIT. On the other hand, as indicated earlier, market participants, only engaging in transactions referred to in Article 5(1)(b), 5(1)(c) or 5(1)(d) of the REMIT Implementing Regulation, hence not required to register with their NRA pursuant to Article 9(1) of REMIT, fall outside the perimeter of market participants subject to the exposure reporting obligation. Counterparties to such transactions that are themselves registered market participants shall not include the positions resulting from such transactions into their monthly position calculation, but under their forecasted production (and potentially consumption) information to be reported upon request. Estimations in the position report

Market participants are expected to provide estimates when calculating their trading positions only when the nature of the traded contract considered for the position calculation requires it, as for the case of some non-standard contracts with variable delivery options. In such cases, it may be necessary to provide estimates on the traded volume when transposing it to the relevant 18-month delivery window. For further guidance on cases when estimations are expected, see below. Market participants must always refer to this guidance to seek understanding on the particular trading scenarios where estimates may be accepted.

units.b: Individual versus intragroup positions – Group assessment
units.t:
As indicated in Article 6(3)(d) of the REMIT Implementing Regulation, the position of market participants shall be differentiated between intragroup and non-intragroup positions when reported to ACER. This means that for the purpose of the position reporting market participants shall calculate separately whether the position refers to a trading activity within a group or not. The prerequisite for performing such differentiation is to determine the definition of a ‘group’ in the context of position reporting under REMIT. It is ACER’s view that market participants must establish individually how they want to define their own group perimeter as regards managing exposures, in order to fulfil their exposure reporting obligation under REMIT with regards to intragroup positions. The information on whether the market participant reporting exposure is part of a group for the sake of the exposure calculation has to be provided in Data Field (2) and Data Field (3) in the electronic format. In particular, market participants must choose one of the following options to indicate how they wish to define their own group perimeter.

Option 1 can be chosen by the reporting market participant even if it had not concluded transactions with all its intragroup members listed in its Central European Register of Energy Market Participants (CEREMP) profile. It is important to note that Option 2 shall be understood as a group perimeter for indicating a group of entities effectively managing their exposures together. Furthermore, selecting Option 2 shall not mean that market participants need to adjust their group definition in CEREMP accordingly. For example, a market participant may be associated in ownership with a TSO or even a competitor. It is at the market participants’ discretion to choose among the three options the one that best reflects the exposure-related situation in practice. However, the reporting market participant shall ensure that its counterparty or counterparties with whom the reporting market participant concludes transactions falling under the scope of Article 5(1)(a) of the REMIT Implementing Regulation appear in the chosen group perimeter. This means that if selecting Option 1, the counterparty shall be identified in CEREMP as a group member of the reporting market participant, while if Option 2 is chosen, the counterparty shall be listed and identified in Data Field (3) together with the reporting market participant. The market participant may select its preferred option for defining its group perimeter for each reference quarter and may change this selection for subsequent reference quarters as desired, from among the options described above. Intragroup transactions under exposure reporting
As described above, market participants need to define their group perimeter for the purpose of exposure reporting under REMIT by choosing one of the three options presented above. It is important to note that when, at the cut-off date, in the given reference quarter the market participant takes into consideration the relevant contracts to be included in the position calculation, the mandatory differentiation between intragroup and non-intragroup positions shall be carried out according to the chosen group perimeter (i.e. Option 1, Option 2 or Option 3) reported in Data Fields (2) and (3).

The position per delivery country has to be calculated by considering all financial and physical futures/forwards, irrespective of where and how the trading activity is conducted. This also includes contracts that are executed on non-MiFID II ( ) regulated platforms, brokered though EU organised trading facilities, brokered over the counter and agreed bilaterally. For contracts such as spreads and swaps, the positions relating to the individual buy and sell legs shall be taken into account for the position calculation and shall be considered as contract type forwards or futures. For options, market participants should report positions irrespective of whether the instrument is ‘in-the-money’. The reported volume should correspond to the contractual notional volume of the underlying commodity. When compiling positions, market participants should align the signs with the table provided in Section 3.4, depending on whether the option is a put or a call option, and whether they are acting on the buy or sell side. If by the end of a particular cut-off date for the position calculation the option is exercised and results, for example, in a futures position, then this position is to be reported. If the instrument cannot be exercised anymore, it shall not be taken into consideration for the position calculation. As indicated earlier, trading up to and including the cut-off date should also be taken into account in case of options. When considering the contracts to be considered for the calculation of the position reporting, some are considered out of scope, such as:
• contracts traded in the intraday and day-ahead markets and contracts, where the delivery period is one week or less (for electricity and natural gas, but not including LNG);
• Electricity Price Area Differentials (EPAD) contracts (because they relate just to a specific zone within a country).

The traded volumes (as a result of the correct aggregation as described above) shall be calculated by netting the purchase (positive sign, plus +) and the sell (negative sign, minus –) positions of the market participant. The resulting traded volume netted shall be reported in the position report per contract type. In general, the following sign convention shall be considered for the position calculation.
Exposure type/sign | + (plus) | – (minus)
Position | Long | Short
For options, the table below should be considered for the calculation of the net traded volumes.
Option/transaction type | Long (buy option) | Short (sell option)
Call (right to buy) | + | –
Put (right to sell) | – | +
As explained above, if the market participant has no traded volume in a delivery month included in the 18-month delivery window for the given delivery country, value ‘NA’ for ‘Not applicable’ shall be reported for that month in the electronic format. This requirement does not apply in relation to the delivery country (i.e. no need to report the country where the market participant has no position in any of the relevant 18 months).

The differentiation between the intragroup and non-intragroup position reports shall be carried out on the total net trading position per commodity, per delivery month, per delivery country, and also split by contract type. For more information on the interpretation of a ‘group’ for the purpose of exposure reporting, see Section 3.2.

Upon the request of ACER, market participants that are subject to the position reporting obligation set out in Article 6(1) of the REMIT Implementing Regulation shall provide the following information:
• forecasted monthly volume of electricity or natural gas production per delivery point or zone and for the reporting period as defined by ACER; and
• forecasted monthly volume of electricity or natural gas consumption, per delivery point or zone and for the reporting period as defined by ACER, based on the market participant’s contracts concluded with its customers. Reporting forecasts on physical elements (forecasted consumption and production), together with positions, are collected solely with the aim of assessing the market participants’ exposure. ACER may issue the requests for the aforementioned forecasts via an open letter or by directly approaching the relevant market participants. The forecasted production and consumption information should only cover volumes that are contractually linked to delivery within the EU. It is acknowledged that forecasts of production and consumption are best estimates based on information available at a given point in time, and thus prone to fluctuations in time (e.g. forecast being volatile in general for intermittent renewable energy sources, planned productions being subject to unexpected interruptions or variations, forecasted consumption being dependent on prices, temperatures). In general, the following sign convention shall be considered when reporting the forecasted productions and consumption volume.
Sign | Plus (+) | Minus (–)
Direction | Incoming (generation) | Outgoing (consumption)
Market participants are expected to provide their best estimates at the time when reporting the forecasts, and to update ( ) them accordingly for subsequent reference quarters if relevant (i.e. in case their estimates have changed in the light of new information). The potential update should relate only to overlapping months in the next reporting cycle. This implies that no periodic obligation to update previously submitted forecasts (e.g. lifecycle events) arises. It is also ACER’s understanding that forecasting future production and consumption is an integral part of business operations. Therefore, market participants are expected to use their own established forecasting practices when carrying out the calculation and aggregation of the forecasted volume as described in this guidance. It is important to note that the cut-off date for the estimation of the forecasted production and consumption, along with the 18-month delivery window, shall be considered applicable as described in Section 2.3. As regards the location of the physical assets, the following two general rules are considered applicable:
• location in the EU: to be reported in full;
• location outside the EU: to be reported just in case (and in the amount) relevant for EU delivery.
Forecast of production
The forecasted monthly volume of electricity or natural gas production shall include the forecast on the market participant’s expected generation. This must also include production outside of the EU but to be delivered in the EU. This means that if the production site is located outside the EU, but the market participant has delivery obligations into the EU, the forecasted production shall be reported by flagging

( ) This requirement does not refer to a lifecycle reporting obligation. the Member State where the produced energy enters the EU (i.e. EU entry country). The information on the forecasted production at production sites located outside the EU shall cover that portion of the forecasted production that is meant to be delivered in the EU. This implies that production volumes that are neither intended for delivery in the EU nor supported by arrangements securing delivery into the EU should fall outside the scope of the forecast. For natural gas, the forecast on the withdrawal of natural gas from storage, including LNG, shall also be considered as production by the market participant that is withdrawing the gas from the facility, provided the market participant effectively holds the relevant storage capacity. For forecasted production of LNG that is produced outside the EU, the country of arrival in the EU (i.e. EU entry country) should be used for the reporting of the forecast. In addition, in terms of delivery country, the LNG cargo should be reported in the country of discharge and not in the country where the LNG, once re-gasified, is intended to be used to fulfil the existing contractual obligations.
Forecast of consumption
The forecasted monthly volume of electricity or natural gas consumption shall include the forecasted consumption of the reporting market participant based on its contracts concluded with its customers, implying that all contracts with consumers have to be included. Market participants should also factor in their own consumption, if applicable, to the forecast. Filling natural gas in storage (i.e. injection) by the market participant shall be counted in the market participant’s forecast for its consumption, provided the market participant effectively holds the relevant storage capacity. Regarding non-EU consumption, this should only be reported insofar as relevant for EU exposure. For example, if a particular intra-EU production is earmarked for export outside of the EU, then this should be reported in full as a generation forecast in the EU, and (partially) offset by reporting this consumption under the Member State where the energy leaves the EU (i.e. EU exit country). This implies that when the energy produced within the EU is destined for export outside the EU, the related consumption should be reported under the relevant EU exit country, namely the country through which the energy leaves the EU. In the context of LNG, when an LNG cargo is being reloaded in the EU for extra-EU exports, the reloaded LNG volume should be considered under the forecasted consumption information marked for the Member State where the cargo is being reloaded for the export.

Market participants shall note that the exposure reporting obligation under REMIT does not refer to individual transactions and, as such, does not include a lifecycle reporting obligation either for positions or forecasts, given that this reporting obligation relates to the market participants’ exposure as of the last day of the reference quarter. This means that exposure information that was calculated by the market participant in the given reference quarter for the next 18 months is not required to be updated based on subsequent adjustments (e.g. due to change of circumstances) that may occur during the delivery period of the related contracts. However, when reporting the same month in the next quarterly report, positions resulting from additional trading activity shall be factored in, if relevant. On the other hand, wrongly reported exposure information must be corrected by the market participant as soon as the market participant discovers or gets notified about the erroneous reporting. For further information, see Data Field (14) Action type. In case there is the need to invalidate a previously submitted exposure report, the relevant market participant is expected to open a contingency through its RRM and indicate the planned actions for resolution.

Market participants shall report their exposure information to ACER via a chosen RRM that is registered by ACER ( ), by using the predefined ISO-aligned electronic format (REMITExposure). For information on how to populate the data fields available in the electronic format, see Chapter 8.

The reported forecasted consumption volume shall be expressed in MWh or GWh. The chosen unit of measurement shall be indicated in Data Field (13) Unit of measurement and applicable for all other volume information reported in the relevant exposure report for the given commodity.

Unit of measurement
<Unit>

MWh Text 3 MWh GWh
The field shall indicate the unit of measurement for the volume information reported in Data Field (10) relevant for positions and, upon request, in Data Fields (11) and (12) for the forecasted production and consumption volume. The volume information reported in the above-mentioned data fields shall be expressed in MWh or GWh. All volumes must be expressed in the same unit measurement chosen for the reporting of both positions and forecasts in the given exposure report. In case of LNG commodity, ACER requests market participants to apply the following conversion criteria for their calculation: MMBtu ≈ 0.293 MWh. The data field is always mandatory.

When an exposure report is submitted to ACER for the first time, it shall always be reported with Action type N for ‘New’. If the exposure report previously submitted has been incorrectly reported, it shall be invalidated by using Action type E for ‘Error’. The corrected report is to be reported with Action type N given that the original N record has been invalidated. In addition, Action type E is also to be used in case the ACER code of a group member is to be corrected in Data Field (3). The data field is always mandatory.
